markers.title: Folate Methylation (C677T / Ala222Val)
markers.mechanism: C677T (Ala222Val) destabilizes the MTHFR enzyme. Heterozygotes (CT) retain ~65% activity; homozygotes (TT) retain ~30% activity, especially under low riboflavin (B2). Slower production of 5-MTHF impairs homocysteine remethylation.

CC.label: Typical MTHFR activity (CC)
CC.summary: Both copies are the wild-type C allele. Folate conversion to 5-MTHF proceeds normally.
CC.detail: No genetic bottleneck at C677T. Folate requirements can be met with standard dietary leafy greens, legumes, and whole foods.

eat: Maintain balanced leafy green vegetables and legume intake. No need for specialized high-dose methylfolate from this SNP.

CT.label: Intermediate MTHFR activity (CT)
CT.summary: One T copy. Enzyme stability is moderately reduced (~65% residual activity).
CT.detail: Slightly higher sensitivity to low dietary folate or low riboflavin (B2, the MTHFR cofactor). Usually clinically silent unless dietary intake is low.

eat: Prioritize folate-rich foods (spinach, arugula, lentils, eggs) and dietary riboflavin.
If supplementing B vitamins, a modest active B-complex is generally well tolerated.

TT.label: Reduced MTHFR activity (TT)
TT.summary: TT homozygote. Enzyme activity drops to ~30%, significantly slowing conversion of folate into active 5-MTHF.
TT.detail: Most strongly associated with elevated plasma homocysteine when dietary folate or riboflavin is low. Not a disease, but requires proactive nutritional attention. Megadoses of synthetic folic acid can lead to unmetabolized folic acid in plasma.

eat: Prioritize natural folates (leafy greens, liver, legumes) and dietary riboflavin (eggs, dairy, almonds).
Avoid heavy consumption of foods fortified with high-dose synthetic folic acid.
Include natural choline sources (pastured egg yolks, sunflower lecithin) to support the alternate BHMT remethylation pathway.
recover: Discuss a fasting homocysteine blood panel with your physician if cardiovascular or reproductive health is a focus.

markers.notes: Effect is highly nutrient-dependent. Pair with MTHFR A1298C, MTRR, and PEMT for a complete 1-carbon read.

markers.title: Folate Methylation (A1298C / Glu429Ala)
markers.mechanism: A1298C sits in the C-terminal regulatory domain of MTHFR. By itself it causes a minor reduction in enzyme activity (~80% in CC), but compound heterozygosity (677CT + 1298AC) has an additive effect.

AA.label: Typical (AA)
AA.summary: No A1298C variant. Normal regulatory domain function.
AA.detail: Standard dietary folate needs.

AC.label: Heterozygote (AC)
AC.summary: One C copy. Very mild effect in isolation.
AC.detail: In the absence of C677T variants, this is considered a typical variation with minimal clinical significance.

eat: Standard whole food diet with regular green vegetables.

CC.label: A1298C Homozygote (CC)
CC.summary: Two C copies. Mildly reduced MTHFR regulation and tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) coupling.
CC.detail: May have a modest effect on neurotransmitter cofactor recycling (BH4) when oxidative stress is high. Less potent than C677T TT on homocysteine.

eat: Emphasize antioxidant-rich foods, dark berries, and leafy greens to support BH4 and nitric oxide coupling.

markers.notes: Evaluate together with C677T rather than in isolation.

markers.title: Methionine Synthase Reductase (A66G / Ile22Met)
markers.mechanism: MTRR maintains the active, reduced state of Methionine Synthase (MTR, Cob(I)alamin). The 66G variant reduces MTRR efficiency, requiring higher cellular B12 availability to maintain homocysteine clearance.

AA.label: Typical MTRR (AA)
AA.summary: Normal cobalamin reduction efficiency.
AA.detail: Standard B12 dietary requirements.

AG.label: MTRR Heterozygote (AG)
AG.summary: One G allele. Mild reduction in MTR reactivation.
AG.detail: Adequate dietary B12 prevents any functional impairment.

eat: Ensure consistent dietary intake of bioavailable B12 (fish, poultry, eggs, dairy or fortified sources).

GG.label: Reduced MTRR Efficiency (GG)
GG.summary: Two G alleles. Lower efficiency in maintaining active vitamin B12 in the methionine synthase cycle.
GG.detail: Can contribute to elevated homocysteine if active B12 (methylcobalamin/adenosylcobalamin) levels are suboptimal.

eat: Ensure robust active B12 intake. If plant-based, utilize sublingual methylcobalamin/adenosylcobalamin rather than basic cyanocobalamin.

markers.notes: Crucial cofactor enzyme linking the folate and methionine cycles.

markers.title: Methionine Synthase (A2756G / Asp919Gly)
markers.mechanism: MTR catalyzes the transfer of a methyl group from 5-methyltetrahydrofolate to homocysteine, forming methionine and tetrahydrofolate. The G allele is associated with altered homocysteine conversion.

AA.label: Typical (AA)
AA.summary: Common genotype. Standard methionine synthesis rate.
AA.detail: Dietary baseline.

AG.label: Heterozygote (AG)
AG.summary: One G allele. Generally balanced enzymatic flux.
AG.detail: Standard nutrition.

GG.label: G Variant (GG)
GG.summary: Homozygous G. Altered MTR kinetics.
GG.detail: Interacts with MTRR and B12 status. High-protein or high-homocysteine states warrant adequate B12 and folate.

eat: Support with balanced choline, betaine (beets, spinach), and active B12.

markers.title: Cystathionine Beta-Synthase (C699T)
markers.mechanism: CBS initiates the transsulfuration pathway, converting homocysteine to cystathionine, leading to glutathione and taurine synthesis. The T allele is an upregulation/gain-of-function variant, accelerating homocysteine clearance toward sulfites and taurine.

CT.label: Mildly Accelerated CBS (CT)
CT.summary: One upregulated T allele.
CT.detail: Slightly faster conversion of homocysteine into the transsulfuration pathway.

TT.label: Accelerated Transsulfuration (TT)
TT.summary: Homozygous upregulation. Homocysteine is rapidly pulled down into transsulfuration.
TT.detail: Can lead to lower baseline homocysteine and higher downstream sulfite/sulfate production. Some individuals may be sensitive to high-sulfur foods or excess crucifers if molybdenum is low.

eat: Ensure adequate dietary molybdenum (legumes, leafy greens) to support sulfite oxidase (SUOX) downstream.

markers.notes: Balances the choice between methyl remethylation vs transsulfuration/glutathione generation.

markers.title: Phosphatidylethanolamine N-Methyltransferase (-744G>C)
markers.mechanism: PEMT synthesizes phosphatidylcholine de novo in the liver using 3 SAMe molecules. Estrogen induces PEMT. Variants reduce endogenous choline synthesis, making dietary choline essential to prevent fatty liver (NAFLD) and muscle damage.

CT.label: Reduced PEMT Capacity (CT)
CT.summary: Heterozygote. Reduced de novo choline production.
CT.detail: Dietary choline becomes more critical, particularly during pregnancy, lactation, or low-estrogen states.

eat: Include 2–3 whole pastured eggs daily, or dietary fish, beef, or sunflower lecithin to supply phosphatidylcholine.

TT.label: High Dietary Choline Requirement (TT)
TT.summary: Homozygous variant. Severely blunted endogenous phosphatidylcholine production.
TT.detail: High susceptibility to hepatic fat accumulation (NAFLD) on low-choline diets. Requires dedicated dietary choline intake.

eat: Prioritize rich dietary choline sources: egg yolks, salmon, organ meats, or sunflower lecithin (target 550+ mg/day).
Crucial for cell membrane integrity, bile flow, and VLDL export from liver.

markers.notes: Key gene linking methylation to liver health, lipid export, and cognitive function.

markers.title: Betaine-Homocysteine Methyltransferase (Arg239Gln)
markers.mechanism: BHMT provides the secondary, folate-independent pathway for remethylating homocysteine using betaine (trimethylglycine).

AA.label: Typical BHMT (AA)
AA.summary: Standard betaine-dependent remethylation.
AA.detail: Normal dietary baseline.

AG.label: Heterozygote (AG)
AG.summary: Intermediate betaine-homocysteine flux.
AG.detail: Standard diet.

GG.label: Altered BHMT (GG)
GG.summary: Altered betaine utilization.
GG.detail: Higher reliance on folate-dependent MTHFR/MTR pathway if betaine/choline intake is low.

eat: Incorporate dietary betaine (beets, quinoa, spinach, wheat bran) to support liver remethylation.

markers.title: Serine Hydroxymethyltransferase (C1420T)
markers.mechanism: SHMT1 directs 1-carbon units between folate-mediated thymidylate synthesis (DNA repair) and homocysteine remethylation.

CC.label: Typical (CC)
CC.detail: Normal DNA synthesis and methylation balance.

CT.label: Heterozygote (CT)
CT.summary: Intermediate 1-carbon flux.
CT.detail: Standard diet.

TT.label: Altered Partitioning (TT)
TT.summary: Shifts folate allocation toward DNA synthesis.
TT.detail: Can slightly lower available 5,10-methyleneTHF for methylation under low-folate conditions.

eat: Maintain high intake of leafy vegetables and natural folates.

markers.title: Choline Transporter-Like Protein 1 (CTL1)
markers.mechanism: SLC44A1 transports choline across cell membranes and into mitochondria for betaine synthesis.

AA.label: Typical Transport (AA)
AA.summary: Standard cellular choline uptake.
AA.detail: Dietary baseline.

AG.label: Heterozygote (AG)
AG.summary: Mild reduction in transport velocity.
AG.detail: Ensure adequate choline intake.

GG.label: Reduced Choline Transport (GG)
GG.summary: Decreased cellular choline uptake capacity.
GG.detail: Increases dietary choline dependency for cognitive acetylcholine and hepatic phospholipid synthesis.

eat: Prioritize bioavailable dietary choline (egg yolks, liver, fish) throughout the day.

markers.title: Apolipoprotein E Cys112Arg (ε4 Determinant)
markers.mechanism: rs429358 combined with rs7412 determines the APOE ε2, ε3, or ε4 isoform. The C allele creates the Arg112 variant (ε4), which alters VLDL/LDL binding, increases circulating LDL particle count, and influences amyloid clearance in the brain.

CC.label: APOE ε4 Present (CC)
CC.summary: Two copies of the ε4 determinant (ε4/ε4 if rs7412 is CC).
CC.detail: Strongly associated with higher average LDL-C/ApoB and increased risk of atherosclerosis and late-onset Alzheimer's. Not a deterministic diagnosis. Lifestyle, metabolic fitness, aerobic exercise, and sleep quality strongly modulate lifetime expression.

eat: Adopt a Mediterranean-style diet high in polyphenols, monounsaturated fats (extra virgin olive oil), and fiber.
Limit excess saturated fat and refined carbohydrates to manage ApoB.
move: Maintain a consistent weekly zone-2 aerobic and strength training regimen to stimulate cerebral blood flow and lipid clearance.
sleep: Prioritize 7.5–8.5 hours of high-quality sleep for optimal glymphatic brain clearance.

CT.label: APOE ε4 Heterozygote (CT)
CT.summary: One copy of the ε4 allele (typically ε3/ε4).
CT.detail: Carries moderate sensitivity to dietary saturated fat with higher average ApoB and cardiovascular risk.

eat: Emphasize extra virgin olive oil, wild fatty fish, high dietary soluble fiber (psyllium, oats, legumes).
Check advanced lipid panel (ApoB, Lp(a), LDL-P) with a physician.
move: Regular aerobic conditioning enhances lipid transport and endothelial function.

TT.label: APOE ε4 Absent (TT)
TT.summary: No ε4 allele at this position (typically ε3/ε3, ε2/ε3, or ε2/ε2 depending on rs7412).
TT.detail: Standard baseline lipid particle clearance and typical neurological risk profile.

eat: Standard cardioprotective dietary pattern.

markers.notes: Must be interpreted in conjunction with rs7412 to identify the true APOE diplotype (ε2/ε2, ε2/ε3, ε3/ε3, ε3/ε4, ε4/ε4, ε2/ε4).

markers.title: Apolipoprotein E Arg158Cys (ε2 Determinant)
markers.mechanism: rs7412 determines the ε2 allele (T allele / Cys158). ε2 has defective binding to the LDL receptor (<2% normal affinity), leading to upregulation of hepatic LDL receptors, generally resulting in lower circulating LDL-C.

CC.label: Typical (CC)
CC.summary: Standard Arg158. Forms ε3 or ε4 depending on rs429358.

CT.label: APOE ε2 Heterozygote (CT)
CT.summary: One ε2 allele. Associated with lower average LDL-C and ApoB concentrations.
CT.detail: Generally cardioprotective regarding LDL-mediated atherosclerosis, though triglycerides may be slightly higher.

eat: Maintain balanced triglycerides by limiting refined sugars and alcohol.

TT.label: APOE ε2/ε2 Genotype (TT)
TT.summary: Two ε2 alleles. Substantially reduced LDL receptor binding.
TT.detail: Most individuals have very low LDL-C, but ~5–10% can develop Type III Hyperlipoproteinemia (dysbetalipoproteinemia) if obesity or insulin resistance is present.

eat: Keep insulin sensitivity high; avoid high-sugar diets and excessive alcohol to prevent remnant lipoprotein accumulation.
recover: Monitor fasting triglycerides and VLDL in routine checkups.

markers.notes: Pairs with rs429358 to define the APOE diplotype.

markers.title: Lipoprotein(a) Elevation (KIV-2 Repeat Tag)
markers.mechanism: LPA encodes apolipoprotein(a), which binds LDL to form Lp(a)—an independent, genetically determined driver of cardiovascular disease and calcific aortic stenosis. The G allele is strongly associated with high circulating Lp(a) levels (>50 mg/dL / 125 nmol/L).

AA.label: Typical Lp(a) (AA)
AA.summary: No risk allele detected. Lower baseline probability of genetically high Lp(a).
AA.detail: Diet and lifestyle remain the primary drivers of general cardiovascular health.

AG.label: Elevated Lp(a) Carrier (AG)
AG.summary: One G allele. Associated with elevated plasma Lipoprotein(a).
AG.detail: Lp(a) is predominantly genetically determined and largely resistant to standard statin therapy or diet. Strongly increases lifetime cardiovascular and thrombosis risk.

eat: Strictly manage other modifiable cardiovascular risk factors: blood pressure, ApoB, fasting glucose, and inflammation.
recover: Request a one-time quantitative Lp(a) blood test with a physician to establish your exact baseline concentration.

GG.label: High Lp(a) Homozygote (GG)
GG.summary: Two G alleles. Associated with substantially elevated Lp(a) levels.
GG.detail: High lifetime cardiovascular risk from both atherogenic and thrombogenic mechanisms of Lp(a).

eat: Intensive cardiovascular prevention strategy focusing on blood pressure, optimal ApoB, smoking avoidance, and anti-inflammatory lifestyle.
recover: Work closely with a cardiologist or lipid specialist to evaluate Lp(a)-lowering therapies and overall risk management.

markers.notes: Lp(a) is a top independent cardiovascular risk factor that is 90% genetically determined.

markers.title: Lipoprotein(a) I4399M / KIV-2 Variant
markers.mechanism: Another potent functional variant in the LPA gene associated with markedly elevated Lp(a) and increased risk of coronary artery disease and stroke.

CT.label: Elevated Lp(a) (CT)
CT.summary: One C allele. High likelihood of elevated Lp(a).
CT.detail: Independent risk factor for coronary disease and thrombosis.

recover: Measure serum Lp(a) directly to quantify cardiovascular risk.

TT.label: High Lp(a) (CC)
TT.summary: Homozygous C. Substantially elevated Lp(a).
TT.detail: High atherogenic particle burden.

recover: Consult a lipid specialist for comprehensive cardiovascular risk management.

markers.title: Proprotein Convertase Subtilisin/Kexin 9 (R46L / Loss of Function)
markers.mechanism: PCSK9 binds to and degrades LDL receptors on hepatocytes. The T allele is a loss-of-function mutation (R46L) that preserves LDL receptors, leading to lifelong lower LDL-C (~15–30% reduction) and ~40–80% lower lifetime coronary heart disease risk.

GG.label: Typical PCSK9 Activity (GG)
GG.summary: Normal PCSK9 expression and LDL receptor degradation.
GG.detail: Standard lipid management.

GT.label: PCSK9 Loss-of-Function Carrier (GT)
GT.summary: One T allele (R46L). Lifelong lower LDL-C and significantly reduced cardiovascular risk.
GT.detail: Natural genetic equivalent of PCSK9 inhibitor medications. Conveys substantial cardiovascular protection across the lifespan.

eat: Continue healthy dietary habits; you have a favorable genetic buffer for LDL particle clearance.

TT.label: PCSK9 Homozygote Loss-of-Function (TT)
TT.summary: Two T alleles. Markedly lower lifetime LDL-C and profound cardioprotection.
TT.detail: Extremely rare and strongly protective against coronary artery disease.

eat: Maintain overall metabolic health and cardiovascular fitness.

markers.notes: A premier example of a beneficial cardioprotective loss-of-function mutation.

markers.title: Cholesteryl Ester Transfer Protein (TaqIB / Intron 1)
markers.mechanism: CETP transfers cholesteryl esters from HDL to VLDL/LDL. The A allele (B2 allele) is associated with lower CETP activity, resulting in higher circulating HDL-C and favorable longevity associations.

AA.label: Typical CETP (GG)
AA.summary: Higher CETP activity. Standard HDL-C levels.
AA.detail: Normal lipid remodeling.

AG.label: Intermediate CETP (AG)
AG.summary: One A allele. Moderately lower CETP activity and higher average HDL-C.
AG.detail: Favorable lipid profile.

GG.label: Reduced CETP / High HDL (AA)
GG.summary: Two A alleles. Lower CETP activity, higher HDL particle concentration and larger particle size.
GG.detail: Associated in multiple centenarian cohorts with cardiovascular resilience and healthy aging.

eat: Support HDL functionality with polyphenol-rich foods, extra virgin olive oil, and regular exercise.

markers.title: Factor V Leiden (Arg506Gln)
markers.mechanism: Factor V Leiden (G1691A / Arg506Gln) renders Factor Va resistant to cleavage and inactivation by activated protein C (APC resistance), increasing venous thromboembolism (DVT/PE) risk.

CC.label: Typical (CC)
CC.summary: No Factor V Leiden mutation detected. Normal clotting cascade regulation.

CT.label: Factor V Leiden Heterozygote (CT)
CT.summary: One copy of Factor V Leiden. ~3–7x increased lifetime risk of venous thromboembolism (DVT / PE).
CT.detail: Important clinical context: long-haul flights, surgery, immobilization, pregnancy, or estrogen-containing oral contraceptives/HRT significantly amplify clotting risk.

move: Stay active on flights over 4 hours: walk every 90 min, wear compression socks, and stay hydrated.
recover: Inform physicians and surgeons before any procedure or when considering estrogen therapies. Do NOT self-prescribe blood thinners.

TT.label: Factor V Leiden Homozygote (TT)
TT.summary: Two copies of Factor V Leiden. ~50–80x increased lifetime risk of venous thromboembolism.
TT.detail: High risk of thrombosis requiring formal clinical hematology consultation and specialized precautions around surgery and travel.

recover: Must be clinically confirmed with a medical genetic or coagulation panel. Discuss preventive strategies with a hematologist.

markers.notes: The most common inherited thrombophilia in European-ancestry populations.

markers.title: Prothrombin G20210A Mutation
markers.mechanism: A point mutation in the 3' UTR of the Prothrombin (F2) gene that increases mRNA stability and elevates plasma prothrombin levels, raising venous thrombosis risk by ~2–3x in heterozygotes.

AA.label: Typical Prothrombin (GG)
AA.summary: Normal prothrombin regulation.
AA.detail: Baseline clotting risk.

AG.label: Prothrombin 20210A Carrier (AG)
AG.summary: One 20210A allele. Elevated circulating prothrombin and increased venous clotting risk.
AG.detail: Multiplies with other risk factors (smoking, surgery, oral contraceptives, prolonged immobility).

move: Take active walking breaks during long-distance travel and use graduated compression socks.
recover: Inform physicians prior to surgeries or pregnancy.

GG.label: Prothrombin 20210A Homozygote (AA)
GG.summary: Two 20210A alleles. Significantly elevated prothrombin and thrombosis risk.
GG.detail: Requires clinical hematology guidance.

recover: Consult a physician for a formal thrombophilia assessment.

markers.title: 9p21.3 Coronary Artery Disease Risk Locus
markers.mechanism: The 9p21.3 locus near CDKN2A/CDKN2B is the most replicated GWAS locus for coronary artery disease (CAD) and myocardial infarction, acting independently of traditional blood lipid levels.

AA.label: Typical (AA)
AA.summary: No 9p21.3 risk allele.
AA.detail: Standard baseline CAD risk.

AG.label: One 9p21.3 Risk Allele (AG)
AG.summary: One risk allele. ~15–20% increased lifetime risk of CAD.
AG.detail: Acts independently of cholesterol through vascular wall biology and cellular senescence.

eat: Strong adherence to a vascular-protective lifestyle: blood pressure control, regular exercise, and non-smoking.

GG.label: Two 9p21.3 Risk Alleles (GG)
GG.summary: Two risk alleles. ~30–40% increased lifetime risk of CAD.
GG.detail: Significant genetic predisposition for vascular atherosclerosis. Highly responsive to lifestyle risk reduction.

eat: Prioritize optimal blood pressure (<120/80), zero tobacco exposure, and tight metabolic management.

markers.title: 9p21.3 Coronary Artery Disease Tag
markers.mechanism: Complementary tag SNP in the 9p21.3 vascular senescence locus.

CG.label: Heterozygote (CG)
CG.summary: One risk allele for coronary atherosclerosis.

GG.label: Homozygous Risk (CC)
GG.summary: Two risk alleles. Elevated coronary atherosclerosis risk.
GG.detail: Emphasize comprehensive cardiovascular risk reduction.

move: Maintain daily cardiovascular exercise to preserve vascular endothelial elasticity.

markers.title: Endothelial Nitric Oxide Synthase (eNOS / Glu298Asp)
markers.mechanism: eNOS synthesizes nitric oxide (NO) in endothelial cells to regulate vasodilation and vascular tone. The T allele (Asp298) increases susceptibility to enzyme cleavage, reducing basal NO production under oxidative stress.

GG.label: Normal eNOS (GG)
GG.summary: Standard endothelial nitric oxide synthesis.
GG.detail: Normal vascular reactivity.

GT.label: Heterozygote (GT)
GT.summary: Mildly reduced NO synthesis under oxidative conditions.

TT.label: Reduced eNOS Activity (TT)
TT.summary: Two Asp298 alleles. Lower basal endothelial NO production and higher blood pressure sensitivity to oxidative stress.
TT.detail: Endothelial lining benefits significantly from dietary nitrate donors and aerobic exercise.

eat: Incorporate dietary nitrate-rich foods: beets, arugula, pomegranate, and citrus (citrulline/arginine sources).
move: Consistent zone-2 cardiovascular training stimulates eNOS phosphorylation and blood vessel dilation.

markers.title: Angiotensinogen (M235T / Met235Thr)
markers.mechanism: AGT is the precursor of angiotensin I in the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS). The C allele (235T) is associated with higher plasma angiotensinogen levels and salt-sensitive blood pressure.

CT.label: Intermediate Sensitivity (CT)
CT.summary: One 235T allele. Moderate sensitivity to dietary sodium.
CT.detail: Maintain balanced electrolytes.

TT.label: Salt-Sensitive Hypertension Risk (CC)
TT.summary: Homozygous 235T. Elevated baseline plasma angiotensinogen.
TT.detail: Associated with higher risk of salt-sensitive hypertension. High potassium-to-sodium ratio is especially beneficial.

eat: Ensure high dietary potassium (avocados, leafy greens, sweet potatoes) and moderate processed sodium intake.

markers.title: Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme (ACE I/D Proxy)
markers.mechanism: rs4343 is in high linkage disequilibrium with the classic ACE Insertion/Deletion (I/D) polymorphism. The A allele tags the D (Deletion) allele (higher serum ACE activity / power leaning), while G tags the I (Insertion) allele (lower ACE activity / endurance leaning).

AA.label: ACE I-Tag Homozygote (GG)
AA.summary: Tags ACE II genotype. Lower circulating ACE and angiotensin II, higher bradykinin levels.
AA.detail: Associated with enhanced muscle efficiency, capillary density, and endurance performance.

move: Naturally predisposed toward aerobic endurance and sustained fatigue resistance.

AG.label: ACE Heterozygote (AG)
AG.summary: Tags ACE ID genotype. Balanced power and endurance traits.
AG.detail: Balanced athletic potential.

GG.label: ACE D-Tag Homozygote (AA)
GG.summary: Tags ACE DD genotype. Higher circulating ACE activity.
GG.detail: Associated with greater muscular power output and sprint performance, but also slightly higher blood pressure reactivity.

move: Naturally predisposed toward sprint, resistance, and explosive power adaptation.
recover: Monitor resting blood pressure during heavy training blocks.

markers.title: CYP2C19*2 Loss-of-Function Variant (681G>A)
markers.mechanism: CYP2C19*2 is a splicing defect causing complete loss of enzyme activity. CYP2C19 metabolizes clopidogrel (Plavix, bioactivation required), SSRIs (citalopram, escitalopram, sertraline), and proton pump inhibitors (omeprazole, pantoprazole).

AA.label: CYP2C19*2 Homozygote / Poor Metabolizer (AA)
AA.summary: Two loss-of-function alleles (*2/*2). CYP2C19 Poor Metabolizer phenotype.
AA.detail: CPIC Guideline Alert: Ineffective bioactivation of clopidogrel (Plavix) after coronary stenting—alternative antiplatelet therapy (ticagrelor/prasugrel) is recommended by CPIC. Slower clearance of escitalopram and omeprazole.

recover: Critical: Discuss with your physician or pharmacist before taking clopidogrel (Plavix), PPIs, or SSRIs. Never alter medications independently.

AG.label: CYP2C19*2 Heterozygote / Intermediate Metabolizer (AG)
AG.summary: One loss-of-function allele (*1/*2). CYP2C19 Intermediate Metabolizer phenotype.
AG.detail: Reduced activation of clopidogrel and moderately reduced clearance of certain antidepressants and PPIs.

recover: CPIC guidelines recommend evaluating antiplatelet choices with a physician if coronary interventions are planned.

GG.label: Typical CYP2C19 Function (GG)
GG.summary: No *2 variant detected (*1/*1 unless other rare star alleles are present).
GG.detail: Normal expected drug bioactivation and clearance for CYP2C19 substrates.

markers.notes: A premier CPIC Level-1A pharmacogenomic marker.

markers.title: CYP2C19*3 Loss-of-Function Variant (636G>A)
markers.mechanism: CYP2C19*3 creates a premature stop codon (Trp212Ter), abolishing enzyme activity. Prevalent in East Asian populations (~5–10%).

AA.label: CYP2C19*3 Carrier / Reduced Metabolism (AG)
AA.summary: One *3 loss-of-function allele. Intermediate or Poor metabolizer phenotype.
AA.detail: CPIC Guidelines: Reduced clopidogrel activation and reduced clearance of diazepam, omeprazole, and citalopram.

recover: Review with a clinical pharmacist prior to antiplatelet or psychiatric prescriptions.

AG.label: CYP2C19*3 Homozygote / Poor Metabolizer (AA)
AG.summary: Two *3 alleles. Poor metabolizer phenotype.
AG.detail: Substantially reduced clopidogrel bioactivation.

recover: Consult your physician for CPIC-guided alternative antiplatelet selection.

GG.label: Typical (GG)
GG.summary: No *3 variant detected.
GG.detail: Normal baseline.

markers.title: CYP2C19*17 Gain-of-Function Variant (-806C>T)
markers.mechanism: CYP2C19*17 is a promoter variant that increases gene transcription, resulting in Rapid (*1/*17) or Ultrarapid (*17/*17) metabolism.

CC.label: CYP2C19*17 Homozygote / Ultrarapid Metabolizer (TT)
CC.summary: Two *17 alleles. CYP2C19 Ultrarapid Metabolizer phenotype.
CC.detail: Clears PPIs (omeprazole) and certain antidepressants (escitalopram, sertraline) much faster than normal, potentially leading to treatment failure at standard dosages.

recover: Inform prescribing physicians if stomach acid or depression treatments fail to achieve expected clinical response.

CT.label: CYP2C19*17 Heterozygote / Rapid Metabolizer (CT)
CT.summary: One *17 allele. Rapid Metabolizer phenotype.
CT.detail: Moderately faster clearance of CYP2C19 substrates.

recover: Standard clinical monitoring.

TT.label: Typical (CC)
TT.summary: No *17 allele detected.
TT.detail: Normal transcription.

markers.title: CYP2C9*2 Reduced-Function Variant (Arg144Cys)
markers.mechanism: CYP2C9 metabolizes warfarin (Coumadin), phenytoin (Dilantin), celecoxib (Celebrex), and NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen). The *2 allele (T) reduces enzyme activity by ~30–50%.

CC.label: CYP2C9*2 Carrier (CT)
CC.detail: CPIC Guideline: Slower clearance of warfarin and NSAIDs. Warfarin dose requirements are typically lower; standard doses increase bleeding risk.

recover: Alert your clinician if prescribed warfarin; genetic dose-prediction algorithms can prevent bleeding complications.

CT.label: CYP2C9*2 Homozygote (TT)
CT.summary: Two *2 alleles. Significantly reduced CYP2C9 clearance.
CT.detail: Markedly lower warfarin dose requirement and prolonged half-life of NSAIDs and sulfonylureas.

recover: Clinical consultation essential for anticoagulant and anti-inflammatory dosing.

TT.label: Typical (CC)
TT.summary: No *2 variant detected.
TT.detail: Normal baseline clearance.

markers.title: CYP2C9*3 Loss-of-Function Variant (Ile359Leu)
markers.mechanism: The *3 allele (C) reduces CYP2C9 enzyme activity by ~80–90%, dramatically decreasing clearance of warfarin and celecoxib.

AA.label: CYP2C9*3 Carrier (AC)
AA.summary: One *3 allele. CYP2C9 Intermediate to Poor Metabolizer.
AA.detail: CPIC Guideline: Substantially reduced warfarin metabolism, higher sensitivity, and increased bleeding hazard at standard starting doses.

recover: Inform clinicians prior to warfarin, celecoxib, or phenytoin therapy.

AC.label: CYP2C9*3 Homozygote / Poor Metabolizer (CC)
AC.detail: Extreme sensitivity to warfarin and NSAIDs.

recover: Requires specialized clinical dosing algorithms.

markers.title: Vitamin K Epoxide Reductase (-1639G>A)
markers.mechanism: VKORC1 is the target of warfarin. The A allele (-1639A) reduces VKORC1 promoter activity and protein expression, conferring high warfarin sensitivity and requiring significantly lower maintenance doses.

AA.label: High Warfarin Sensitivity (AA)
AA.summary: Two A alleles. Low VKORC1 expression.
AA.detail: CPIC Guideline: Highly sensitive to warfarin. Standard initial doses can cause severe over-anticoagulation and hemorrhage; typical required doses are 50–70% lower.

recover: Crucial clinical info for anticoagulation management. Share with your prescribing doctor.

AG.label: Intermediate Warfarin Sensitivity (AG)
AG.summary: One A allele. Moderate VKORC1 expression.
AG.detail: Requires lower-than-average warfarin maintenance doses.

recover: Standard clinical INR monitoring and dose titration.

GG.label: Standard Warfarin Sensitivity (GG)
GG.summary: Two G alleles. Normal VKORC1 expression.
GG.detail: Typical baseline warfarin dose requirements.

markers.notes: Pairs directly with CYP2C9 to determine personalized warfarin dosing.

markers.title: CYP2D6*4 Splicing Defect (1846G>A)
markers.mechanism: CYP2D6*4 (A) is the most common loss-of-function allele in Europeans. CYP2D6 metabolizes ~25% of all clinical drugs: codeine/tramadol (prodrug activation), tamoxifen, beta-blockers (metoprolol), and antidepressants (venlafaxine, TCAs).

AA.label: CYP2D6*4 Homozygote / Poor Metabolizer (AA)
AA.summary: Two *4 null alleles. CYP2D6 Poor Metabolizer phenotype.
AA.detail: CPIC Guideline: Inability to convert codeine and tramadol into active morphine/M1 (lack of pain relief). Ineffective activation of tamoxifen for breast cancer. Slow clearance of metoprolol and TCAs (higher drug levels/side effects).

recover: Essential medical note: Report CYP2D6 Poor Metabolizer status to your doctor when discussing pain medications, antidepressants, or oncology therapies.

AG.label: CYP2D6*4 Carrier / Intermediate Metabolizer (AG)
AG.summary: One *4 null allele. CYP2D6 Intermediate Metabolizer.
AG.detail: Reduced bioactivation of prodrugs and moderately slowed clearance of substrates.

recover: Discuss appropriate pain management and beta-blocker dosing with a physician.

GG.label: Typical (GG)
GG.summary: No *4 allele detected.
GG.detail: Normal baseline enzyme function.

markers.title: Organic Anion Transporter OATP1B1 (521T>C / *5)
markers.mechanism: SLCO1B1 encodes the OATP1B1 hepatic uptake transporter. The C allele (521C / *5) reduces hepatic uptake of statins (especially simvastatin and atorvastatin), raising systemic plasma statin exposure and significantly increasing risk of statin-induced myopathy/rhabdomyolysis.

CC.label: High Statin Myopathy Risk (CC)
CC.summary: Two C alleles (*5/*5). Severely reduced hepatic statin uptake.
CC.detail: CPIC Guideline: ~15–20x higher risk of statin-induced muscle pain and myopathy with simvastatin. CPIC recommends avoiding high-dose simvastatin and considering alternative statins (pravastatin, rosuvastatin) or lower doses.

recover: Never stop a prescribed statin abruptly. Discuss SLCO1B1 status with your physician to select the safest statin type and dose.

CT.label: Moderate Statin Myopathy Risk (CT)
CT.summary: One C allele (*1/*5). Moderately reduced hepatic statin uptake.
CT.detail: CPIC Guideline: ~4–5x increased risk of simvastatin-induced muscle toxicity.

recover: Inform your doctor if starting statin therapy; lower doses or alternative statins may be preferred.

TT.label: Typical Statin Uptake (TT)
TT.summary: Two T alleles. Normal hepatic OATP1B1 transporter function.
TT.detail: Standard baseline tolerance for statin medications.

markers.notes: Premier CPIC Level-1A guideline for statin safety.

markers.title: Dihydropyrimidine Dehydrogenase (DPYD*2A / IVS14+1G>A)
markers.mechanism: DPYD metabolizes fluoropyrimidine chemotherapies (5-Fluorouracil, Capecitabine). The *2A allele (A) causes complete loss of enzyme activity, leading to lethal drug toxicity if given standard chemotherapy doses.

AA.label: Severe Fluoropyrimidine Toxicity Risk (AA)
AA.summary: Two *2A null alleles. Complete DPYD deficiency.
AA.detail: CPIC Guideline: Absolute contraindication for standard 5-FU / Capecitabine due to life-threatening myelosuppression and GI toxicity.

recover: Critical oncology warning: Must be communicated to oncologist before any fluoropyrimidine chemotherapy.

AG.label: High Toxicity Risk Carrier (AG)
AG.summary: One *2A null allele. DPYD Intermediate Metabolizer (~50% activity).
AG.detail: CPIC Guideline: Requires 50% initial dose reduction of 5-FU/capecitabine with therapeutic drug monitoring to prevent severe toxicity.

recover: Mandatory oncology consultation if considering chemotherapy.

GG.label: Typical DPYD Activity (GG)
GG.summary: No *2A mutation detected.
GG.detail: Normal fluoropyrimidine clearance.

markers.title: Thiopurine S-Methyltransferase (TPMT*3B / 460G>A)
markers.mechanism: TPMT inactivates thiopurine immunosuppressants (Azathioprine, 6-Mercaptopurine). Deficient alleles cause bone marrow suppression (severe leukopenia).

AA.label: Typical TPMT (GG)
AA.summary: Normal thiopurine inactivation.
AA.detail: Standard dosing baseline.

AG.label: Reduced TPMT Activity (AG)
AG.summary: One non-functional allele. TPMT Intermediate Metabolizer.
AG.detail: CPIC Guideline: Requires 30–70% reduction in azathioprine/6-MP starting dose to avoid life-threatening bone marrow toxicity.

recover: Inform gastroenterologist, rheumatologist, or oncologist before thiopurine therapy.

GG.label: Severe TPMT Deficiency (AA)
GG.summary: Two non-functional alleles. TPMT Poor Metabolizer.
GG.detail: CPIC Guideline: Severe myelosuppression risk; requires 90% dose reduction or alternative agents.

recover: Clinical consultation required prior to immunosuppressive thiopurine therapy.

markers.title: UDP-Glucuronosyltransferase 1A1 (UGT1A1*28 / *80 Proxy)
markers.mechanism: UGT1A1 conjugates bilirubin and active drug metabolites (e.g. SN-38 from irinotecan chemotherapy). The T allele tags the *28 TA-repeat expansion in the promoter, causing Gilbert's syndrome (benign unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia) and irinotecan toxicity.

CT.label: Gilbert's Syndrome Carrier (CT)
CT.summary: One *28 tag allele. Mildly reduced glucuronidation.
CT.detail: Generally asymptomatic; occasional mild bilirubin elevations during fasting or illness.

TT.label: Gilbert's Syndrome / Irinotecan Sensitivity (TT)
TT.summary: Two *28 tag alleles. ~70% reduction in UGT1A1 promoter activity.
TT.detail: Classic Gilbert's syndrome: benign mild jaundice during fasting, dehydration, or strenuous exercise. CPIC Alert: Increased toxicity risk with the cancer drug irinotecan.

eat: Stay well-hydrated and avoid prolonged severe fasting if you experience yellowing of the eyes.

markers.title: HLA-B*5701 Tag SNP (Abacavir Hypersensitivity)
markers.mechanism: rs2395029 is in near-perfect linkage disequilibrium with the HLA-B*5701 allele. HLA-B*5701 carriers suffer severe, potentially fatal multi-organ hypersensitivity reactions to the HIV antiretroviral drug Abacavir.

GG.label: Typical (GG)
GG.summary: Negative for HLA-B*5701 tag.
GG.detail: Standard low risk for abacavir hypersensitivity.

GT.label: HLA-B*5701 Positive Tag (GT)
GT.summary: One T allele. Strong tag for HLA-B*5701.
GT.detail: FDA / CPIC Black Box Warning: Abacavir is strictly contraindicated due to severe hypersensitivity reaction risk.

recover: Inform medical providers: HLA-B*5701 positive tag. Never take Abacavir.

TT.label: HLA-B*5701 Homozygote Tag (TT)
TT.summary: Two T alleles. Positive for HLA-B*5701.
TT.detail: Abacavir is strictly contraindicated.

recover: Mandatory medical documentation: Avoid Abacavir.

markers.title: Cytochrome P450 1A2 (Caffeine & Drug Clearance / *1F)
markers.mechanism: CYP1A2 clears caffeine, theophylline, melatonin, and antipsychotics (olanzapine, clozapine). The A allele (*1F) confers high inducibility and fast clearance, whereas the C allele causes slow clearance.

AA.label: Fast Caffeine & Drug Metabolizer (AA)
AA.summary: Two A alleles (*1F/*1F). Highly inducible CYP1A2.
AA.detail: Rapid caffeine clearance (half-life ~2.5–4 hours). Moderate coffee consumption is cardioprotective in fast metabolizers and unlikely to impair sleep if consumed early.

substances: Can tolerate moderate morning coffee with rapid hepatic clearance.

AC.label: Intermediate Metabolizer (AC)
AC.summary: One C allele. Intermediate clearance rate.

substances: Maintain an 8-hour caffeine cutoff before bedtime.

CC.label: Slow Caffeine Metabolizer (CC)
CC.summary: Two C alleles. Slower CYP1A2 clearance (half-life ~7–10 hours).
CC.detail: Caffeine lingers in circulation. High coffee intake (>2–3 cups/day) in slow metabolizers is associated with higher resting blood pressure and increased myocardial infarction risk.

substances: Limit to 1 cup in the early morning or switch to green tea/decaf.
sleep: Caffeine significantly disrupts slow-wave deep sleep in slow metabolizers.

markers.title: Catechol-O-Methyltransferase (Val158Met / Warrior vs Worrier)
markers.mechanism: COMT degrades dopamine, epinephrine, and norepinephrine in the prefrontal cortex (PFC). The A allele (Met158) is thermolabile and has 3–4x lower enzymatic activity, resulting in higher PFC dopamine levels (Worrier phenotype), while the G allele (Val158) clears dopamine rapidly (Warrior phenotype).

AA.label: Met/Met Homozygote / High Dopamine 'Worrier' (AA)
AA.summary: Two Met alleles. Low COMT activity leading to high baseline prefrontal dopamine.
AA.detail: Advantages: Superior working memory, executive focus, attention to detail, and complex cognitive processing in calm environments. Vulnerabilities: Heightened stress reactivity, emotional amplification under high pressure, and slower recovery from catecholamine spikes.

mind: Practice breathwork, progressive relaxation, and stress-buffering routines before high-stakes tasks.
Avoid excessive stimulants (high caffeine, yohimbine) that overload dopamine receptors.
eat: Ensure adequate magnesium to support COMT cofactor function.
High-dose methyl donors can exacerbate anxiety in Met/Met individuals; use conservative doses.

AG.label: Val/Met Heterozygote / Balanced Phenotype (AG)
AG.summary: One Val and one Met allele. Intermediate COMT activity.
AG.detail: Combines good baseline cognitive focus with solid psychological resilience under moderate stress.

mind: Well-balanced dopamine kinetics; adapts well across diverse working conditions.

GG.label: Val/Val Homozygote / Rapid Clearance 'Warrior' (GG)
GG.summary: Two Val alleles. High COMT activity with rapid dopamine and catecholamine breakdown.
GG.detail: Advantages: Outstanding stress resilience, calmness under extreme pressure, and fast recovery from acute stressors. Vulnerabilities: Lower baseline prefrontal dopamine; may experience boredom or lower sustained focus in routine, low-stimulation tasks.

mind: Thrives in high-intensity, dynamic, fast-paced environments.
move: High-intensity interval training (HIIT) and competitive athletics effectively stimulate dopamine.
eat: Protein-rich meals providing tyrosine support steady dopamine synthesis.

markers.notes: The definitive cognitive trade-off polymorphism in human neuroscience.

markers.title: Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor (Val66Met)
markers.mechanism: BDNF governs neurogenesis, synaptic plasticity, and long-term memory consolidation in the hippocampus. The T allele (Met66) impairs activity-dependent secretion of BDNF.

CC.label: Typical BDNF Plasticity (CC)
CC.summary: Val/Val homozygote. Robust activity-dependent BDNF secretion.
CC.detail: Standard hippocampal synaptic plasticity and memory formation.

move: Aerobic exercise further enhances already healthy BDNF expression.

CT.label: Reduced BDNF Secretion / Met Carrier (CT)
CT.summary: Val/Met heterozygote. ~25% reduction in activity-dependent BDNF release.
CT.detail: Moderately lower hippocampal volume and vulnerability to stress-induced cognitive fatigue. Exercise is a potent epigenetic trigger to restore BDNF secretion.

move: Prioritize 3–4 sessions/week of aerobic exercise and resistance training—physical activity is the strongest natural inducer of BDNF.
mind: Incorporate cognitive novelty, continuous learning, and meditation to drive neuroplasticity.
eat: Omega-3 DHA (wild fish or algae) and dietary polyphenols (blueberries, cacao) support neurotrophin signaling.

TT.label: Met/Met Homozygote (TT)
TT.summary: Two Met alleles. Significantly blunted activity-dependent BDNF secretion.
TT.detail: Higher susceptibility to anxiety and impaired memory consolidation under chronic stress.

move: Daily physical exercise is non-negotiable for brain health and mood stability.
sleep: High-quality sleep is critical for synaptic consolidation.
eat: Supplement with high-quality EPA/DHA and dietary antioxidants.

markers.title: Dopamine D2 Receptor Density (Taq1A)
markers.mechanism: The A allele (A1 allele) is associated with a 30–40% reduction in striatal Dopamine D2 receptor binding sites, predisposing to 'Reward Deficiency Syndrome' (higher propensity for food cravings, compulsive behaviors, or substance seeking).

AA.label: Reduced D2 Receptor Density / A1 Carrier (AA)
AA.summary: Two A1 alleles. Substantially reduced dopamine D2 receptor density in striatal reward centers.
AA.detail: Prone to seek external reward stimulation: sweet/fatty comfort foods, excessive gaming, or substance use to achieve normal dopamine satisfaction.

eat: Keep structured, whole-food protein meals to prevent dopamine-seeking snacking on hyperpalatable junk food.
move: Engage in regular strength training and intense sports to provide healthy, natural dopamine surges.
substances: Be strictly mindful with alcohol, nicotine, and gambling.

AG.label: Intermediate D2 Density / A1 Heterozygote (AG)
AG.summary: One A1 allele. Moderately reduced D2 receptor density.
AG.detail: Mild vulnerability to impulsive reward-seeking under stress.

eat: Maintain predictable eating routines and avoid keeping ultra-processed junk food at home.

GG.label: Normal D2 Receptor Density (GG)
GG.summary: Two A2 alleles. Standard baseline dopamine D2 receptor density.
GG.detail: Typical satiety response and healthy baseline reward signaling.

markers.title: Oxytocin Receptor (Empathy & Social Resilience)
markers.mechanism: OXTR mediates the prosocial and stress-buffering effects of oxytocin. The G allele is linked to higher empathy, positive affect, and lower cortisol reactivity to social stress, whereas the A allele confers lower baseline social buffering.

AA.label: High Social Buffering (GG)
AA.summary: Two G alleles. Robust oxytocin receptor expression.
AA.detail: High baseline social empathy, emotional connectedness, and strong stress-buffering from social support.

mind: Cultivate deep interpersonal relationships and community connection.

AG.label: Intermediate OXTR (AG)
AG.summary: One A allele. Balanced social reactivity.
AG.detail: Standard psychological resilience.

GG.label: Lower Social Buffering (AA)
GG.summary: Two A alleles. Lower oxytocin receptor expression.
GG.detail: May feel less naturally buffered by social reassurance during acute stress; benefits from deliberate cognitive reframing.

mind: Practice individual grounding routines, journaling, and dedicated solitary recovery.

markers.title: Glucocorticoid Receptor Sensitivity & Stress Reactivity
markers.mechanism: FKBP5 regulates the sensitivity of the glucocorticoid receptor to cortisol. The T allele promotes hyper-responsiveness of the HPA axis, prolonging cortisol elevation after acute stress.

CT.label: Heightened Cortisol Reactivity (CT)
CT.summary: One T allele. Moderately prolonged cortisol response.
CT.detail: Benefits from deliberate post-stress recovery practices.

mind: Engage in daily parasympathetic breathing (4-7-8 breath) and evening wind-down routines.

TT.label: High Stress Sensitivity (TT)
TT.summary: Two T alleles. Sensitized HPA axis.
TT.detail: Prolonged cortisol elevation after psychological or physical stressors, predisposing to burnout and sleep disruption.

mind: Prioritize active stress management, nature walks, and regular downtime.
Avoid overtraining during high-stress life periods.
sleep: Keep bedtime consistent to preserve normal diurnal cortisol rhythm.

markers.title: Monoamine Oxidase A (R297R / High vs Low Activity)
markers.mechanism: MAOA breaks down serotonin, dopamine, and norepinephrine in the brain. The G allele is associated with higher MAOA activity (faster monoamine clearance), whereas T is associated with lower activity.

GG.label: High MAOA Activity (GG / Hemizygous G)
GG.summary: Rapid monoamine breakdown.
GG.detail: Stable mood baseline, fast clearance of neurotransmitters.

eat: Adequate dietary tryptophan and tyrosine.

GT.label: Intermediate MAOA Activity (GT)
GT.summary: Balanced monoamine breakdown in heterozygous females.

TT.label: Low MAOA Activity (TT / Hemizygous T)
TT.summary: Slower monoamine breakdown.
TT.detail: Neurotransmitters remain active longer. Can be prone to histamine and tyramine sensitivity (aged cheeses, wine).

eat: Moderate intake of high-tyramine fermented foods if headaches or palpitations occur.

markers.title: Circadian Locomotor Output Cycles Kaput (3111T/C / Eveningness)
markers.mechanism: CLOCK is a core transcription factor driving the master cellular circadian rhythm. The G allele (3111C on some strands) is strongly associated with an evening chronotype ('night owl'), delayed sleep phase, and increased vulnerability to metabolic disruption from late-night eating.

AA.label: Typical Morning/Intermediate Chronotype (AA)
AA.summary: Two A alleles. Standard circadian period (~24.1 hours).
AA.detail: Naturally aligned with traditional day-oriented schedules.

sleep: Maintain consistent wake-up times and early daylight exposure.

AG.label: Evening Chronotype Tendency (AG)
AG.summary: One G allele. Shifted circadian phase toward eveningness.
AG.detail: May feel more alert in late evening. Vulnerable to 'social jetlag' if forced onto rigid early schedules.

sleep: Get 15–30 minutes of bright outdoor sunlight immediately upon waking to anchor the circadian clock.
Dim artificial blue lights after 8:30 PM.
eat: Avoid heavy dinners after 8:00 PM to protect insulin sensitivity.

GG.label: Strong Evening Chronotype / Delayed Phase (GG)
GG.summary: Two G alleles. Substantial delay in endogenous melatonin onset and core body temperature drop.
GG.detail: Prone to delayed sleep phase syndrome and circadian misalignment. Late-night snacking causes significantly higher glucose spikes in GG individuals.

sleep: Strict morning light therapy (10,000 lux lamp or direct sunlight for 30 min) to entrain the clock.
Use 100% blue-blocking glasses 2 hours before target sleep time.
eat: Practice strict time-restricted feeding: finish all caloric intake at least 3 hours before sleep.

markers.notes: A master genetic anchor for personalized circadian medicine.

markers.title: Period Circadian Regulator 3 (4/5 Repeat Proxy / Deep Sleep)
markers.mechanism: PER3 regulates homeostatic sleep pressure and slow-wave sleep (N3) architecture. The T allele is linked to higher sleep drive and sensitivity to acute sleep deprivation.

CT.label: Elevated Deep Sleep Drive (CT)
CT.summary: One variant copy. Higher need for restorative slow-wave sleep.
CT.detail: Experiences greater cognitive degradation from sleep restriction.

sleep: Protect an 8-hour sleep window; avoid sacrificing sleep for early morning alarms.

TT.label: High Slow-Wave Sleep Dependency (TT)
TT.summary: Two variant copies. High sensitivity to sleep debt.
TT.detail: Requires consistent, uncompromised sleep duration to maintain executive cognitive function.

sleep: Prioritize a cold, dark sleep sanctuary (65–68°F) to maximize slow-wave recovery.

markers.title: Melatonin Receptor 1B (Late Eating Glucose Disruption)
markers.mechanism: MTNR1B encodes the melatonin receptor on pancreatic beta cells. The G allele increases receptor expression. When melatonin rises in the evening, beta-cell insulin secretion is strongly inhibited. Eating late in the presence of elevated melatonin causes severe glucose spikes in G carriers.

CG.label: Late-Meal Glucose Sensitivity (CG)
CG.summary: One G allele. Heightened beta-cell suppression by melatonin.
CG.detail: Late-night meals (when endogenous melatonin is active) cause markedly higher blood glucose and insulin resistance.

eat: Finish all carbohydrate and heavy food intake at least 2.5–3 hours before bed.
Avoid midnight snacking.

GG.label: Severe Late-Meal Glucose Intolerance (GG)
GG.summary: Two G alleles. High beta-cell melatonin sensitivity; ~1.5x increased Type 2 Diabetes risk.
GG.detail: Direct gene-environment interaction: daytime carbohydrate tolerance is normal, but nighttime carbohydrate tolerance is severely compromised.

eat: Strict dinner cutoff: no calories within 3–4 hours of sleep.
If eating late, keep meals strictly protein/vegetable based with minimal starch.
sleep: Avoid taking high-dose exogenous melatonin close to meals.

markers.notes: A textbook example of chrono-nutrition and gene-meal timing interactions.

markers.title: Adenosine A2A Receptor (Caffeine-Induced Anxiety & Insomnia)
markers.mechanism: Adenosine binds to ADORA2A receptors in the brain to build sleep pressure. Caffeine is an antagonist. The T allele alters receptor conformation, conferring high sensitivity to caffeine-induced anxiety, panic, and sleep architecture disruption.

CT.label: Moderate Caffeine Sensitivity (CT)
CT.summary: Intermediate receptor sensitivity.
CT.detail: Standard moderate intake.

TT.label: High Caffeine-Induced Anxiety & Jitters (TT)
TT.summary: Two T alleles. Highly sensitive adenosine receptor.
TT.detail: Even modest doses of caffeine (100–200 mg) can trigger heart palpitations, somatic anxiety, restlessness, and severe reductions in slow-wave deep sleep.

substances: Keep caffeine intake under 100 mg/day (e.g. green tea) or eliminate it entirely.
Never consume caffeine in the afternoon.
sleep: Caffeine will severely fragment sleep quality even if you are able to fall asleep.

markers.title: Adenosine Deaminase (Deep Sleep Intensity)
markers.mechanism: ADA breaks down adenosine. The A allele reduces enzyme activity, leading to higher brain adenosine levels and significantly deeper, more consolidated slow-wave sleep.

AA.label: Typical ADA (GG)
AA.summary: Normal adenosine clearance.
AA.detail: Standard sleep depth.

AG.label: Enhanced Deep Sleep Carrier (AG)
AG.summary: One A allele. Higher baseline brain adenosine accumulation.
AG.detail: Associated with deeper, more efficient slow-wave sleep (N3) and greater subjective sleep satisfaction.

sleep: Natural predisposition for restorative, deep sleep.

GG.label: Deep Sleep Homozygote (AA)
GG.summary: Two A alleles. Maximized slow-wave sleep intensity.
GG.detail: High sleep efficiency.

markers.title: Transcription Factor 7-Like 2 (Type 2 Diabetes Locus / Intron 3)
markers.mechanism: TCF7L2 is the strongest and most consistently replicated genetic locus for Type 2 Diabetes worldwide. The T allele impairs GLP-1 signaling, proinsulin processing, and pancreatic beta-cell insulin secretion.

CC.label: Typical Diabetes Risk (CC)
CC.detail: Standard baseline risk for Type 2 Diabetes.

CT.label: Elevated Diabetes Susceptibility (CT)
CT.summary: One T allele. ~1.4x increased lifetime risk of Type 2 Diabetes.
CT.detail: Impaired incretin (GLP-1) response and lower beta-cell capacity under chronic glycemic load.

eat: Adopt a low-glycemic, high-fiber dietary pattern to minimize postprandial insulin demand.
Prioritize protein and fiber before starches in meals.
move: Perform post-meal 10–15 minute walks to clear glucose via muscle contraction without requiring insulin.

TT.label: High Diabetes Susceptibility (TT)
TT.summary: Two T alleles. ~2.0x increased lifetime risk of Type 2 Diabetes.
TT.detail: Significant genetic impairment in beta-cell insulin secretory reserve. Highly responsive to lifestyle intervention—exercise and carbohydrate moderation can completely overcome the genetic risk.

eat: Emphasize a low-glycemic Mediterranean or low-carbohydrate approach with generous healthy fats and fiber.
Avoid sugary beverages, refined starches, and ultra-processed carbohydrates.
move: Regular resistance training increases skeletal muscle glucose disposal independent of insulin.
recover: Monitor fasting glucose and HbA1c at annual medical checkups.

markers.notes: The single most important single-SNP predictor of beta-cell vulnerability in human genetics.

markers.title: Peroxisome Proliferator-Activated Receptor Gamma (Pro12Ala)
markers.mechanism: PPARG is the master regulator of adipogenesis and insulin sensitivity (the target of thiazolidinediones). The G allele (Ala12) reduces PPARG transcriptional activity, conferring enhanced insulin sensitivity and ~20% lower Type 2 Diabetes risk.

CC.label: Standard PPARG / Pro12 (CC)
CC.summary: Standard Pro12 allele. Typical adipocyte differentiation.

CG.label: Enhanced Insulin Sensitivity / Ala12 Carrier (CG)
CG.summary: One Ala12 allele. Favorable adipocyte metabolism and enhanced whole-body insulin sensitivity.
CG.detail: Protective against diabetes and metabolic syndrome, particularly when paired with a diet rich in monounsaturated fats.

eat: Extra virgin olive oil, avocados, and nuts actively support PPARG-mediated insulin sensitivity.

GG.label: High Insulin Sensitivity (GG)
GG.summary: Two Ala12 alleles. Highest genetic insulin sensitivity.
GG.detail: Protective against metabolic dysfunction across diverse dietary conditions.

eat: Maintain balanced whole food nutrition.

markers.title: Potassium Inwardly-Rectifying Channel (E23K / Kir6.2)
markers.mechanism: KCNJ11 forms the pore of the ATP-sensitive potassium (K-ATP) channel in pancreatic beta cells. The T allele (Lys23) over-activates the channel, keeping it open and reducing insulin release in response to glucose.

CT.label: Heterozygote (CT)
CT.summary: One Lys23 allele. Mildly blunted insulin secretion.
CT.detail: Standard low-glycemic diet.

TT.label: Reduced Insulin Secretion (TT)
TT.summary: Two Lys23 alleles. Impaired beta-cell glucose-stimulated insulin release.
TT.detail: Contributes to higher postprandial glucose spikes.

eat: Focus on low glycemic index foods, lean proteins, and fiber to prevent sharp glucose spikes.

markers.title: Fat Mass and Obesity-Associated Gene (Appetite & Satiety Signaling)
markers.mechanism: FTO intron 1 variants alter IRX3/IRX5 expression in the hypothalamus and adipose tissue, increasing circulating ghrelin (hunger hormone), blunting post-meal satiety, and promoting caloric intake.

AA.label: Typical Appetite Signaling (TT)
AA.summary: Two T alleles. Standard baseline hunger and satiety regulation.
AA.detail: Baseline obesity risk.

AT.label: Elevated Appetite & Caloric Drive (AT)
AT.summary: One A allele. ~1.2x higher likelihood of higher BMI if diet is unstructured.
AT.detail: Tendency toward larger portion sizes and stronger cravings for calorie-dense foods.

eat: Anchor meals with 30–40g of high-quality protein and high-volume fiber to maximize satiety signals.
Eat meals mindfully without digital distractions.

TT.label: High Caloric Drive / Satiety Deficit (AA)
TT.summary: Two A alleles. Associated with elevated baseline ghrelin and delayed post-meal fullness.
TT.detail: Stronger biological pull toward snacking and hyperpalatable foods. Highly responsive to high-protein diets and physical exercise, which completely normalize the FTO risk.

eat: High-protein dietary strategy (1.6–2.2 g/kg body weight) effectively blunts FTO-mediated hunger.
Avoid liquid calories and keep trigger foods out of the house.
move: Regular physical exercise is proven to attenuate the genetic effect of the FTO risk allele by over 70%.

markers.notes: A major locus for behavioral appetite regulation, heavily modulated by protein intake and movement.

markers.title: Melanocortin 4 Receptor (Hypothalamic Satiety / Obesity Tag)
markers.mechanism: MC4R acts in the leptin-melanocortin satiety pathway in the hypothalamus. The C allele is associated with blunted leptin signaling, higher ad libitum food intake, and increased risk of adiposity.

CT.label: Heterozygote (CT)
CT.summary: One C allele. Moderately reduced satiety signaling.
CT.detail: Benefits from structured meal routines and mindful eating.

eat: Focus on protein, fiber, and structured meal timings.

TT.label: Reduced Satiety Response (CC)
TT.summary: Two C alleles. Impaired fullness signaling.
TT.detail: Prone to continuous snacking and binge eating behavior under stress.

eat: Structured meal planning with designated portion sizes.
Prioritize high-satiety index foods (potatoes, fish, oatmeal, lean meat).

markers.title: Patatin-Like Phospholipase Domain-Containing 3 (I148M / Fatty Liver)
markers.mechanism: PNPLA3 (adiponutrin) mediates triacylglycerol hydrolysis in hepatic lipid droplets. The G allele (148M) impairs enzymatic clearance, leading to hepatic triglyceride accumulation and markedly increased risk of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and alcohol-induced liver damage.

CG.label: Elevated Fatty Liver Susceptibility (CG)
CG.summary: One G allele. ~2x increased risk of hepatic steatosis (NAFLD).
CG.detail: Liver is particularly sensitive to high-fructose corn syrup, refined sugars, and alcohol.

eat: Strictly eliminate sugary drinks, high-fructose corn syrup, and excess refined carbohydrates.
Adopt a Mediterranean diet rich in choline and omega-3s.
substances: Moderate alcohol consumption; avoid heavy drinking episodes.

GG.label: High Fatty Liver & Cirrhosis Risk (GG)
GG.summary: Two G alleles. ~4–5x increased risk of NAFLD, NASH, and hepatic fibrosis.
GG.detail: Pronounced genetic vulnerability to hepatic fat accumulation even at normal body weight (lean NAFLD).

eat: Strict avoidance of added sugars, refined fructose, and ultra-processed seed oils.
Ensure robust dietary choline (eggs) and omega-3 EPA/DHA to support hepatic VLDL secretion.
substances: Strongly advised to minimize or completely eliminate alcohol consumption to protect liver tissue.
recover: Monitor liver enzymes (ALT, AST, GGT) and consider a liver ultrasound/FibroScan in routine checkups.

markers.notes: The single most potent genetic risk factor for hepatic steatosis (fatty liver).

markers.title: Alpha-Actinin-3 (R577X / Sprint vs Endurance)
markers.mechanism: ACTN3 encodes alpha-actinin-3, a structural protein found exclusively in fast-twitch (Type II) muscle fibers that anchors actin filaments and optimizes forceful, explosive muscular contractions. The T allele is a premature stop codon (577X). TT homozygotes produce zero alpha-actinin-3 protein (18% of global population), shifting muscle metabolism toward oxidative endurance.

CC.label: Power / Sprint Specialist (CC / RR)
CC.summary: Two functional R alleles. Full alpha-actinin-3 expression in fast-twitch muscle fibers.
CC.detail: Associated with elite sprint, power, and maximal force production capabilities. Rapid force generation and explosive athletic adaptations.

move: Naturally primed for explosive resistance training, sprinting, Olympic lifting, and power sports.
Include dedicated recovery since fast-twitch fibers produce more post-exercise muscle microtrauma.

CT.label: Balanced Power & Endurance (CT / RX)
CT.summary: One R and one X allele. Intermediate alpha-actinin-3 expression.
CT.detail: Versatile athletic potential across both explosive and endurance disciplines.

move: Responds well to hybrid functional training: strength work combined with aerobic conditioning.

TT.label: Endurance Specialist / Muscle Economy (TT / XX)
TT.summary: Two X null alleles. Zero alpha-actinin-3 protein expression.
TT.detail: Fast-twitch fibers adapt toward oxidative, fatigue-resistant metabolic pathways. Consistently overrepresented among elite marathon runners, cyclists, and endurance athletes.

move: Naturally optimized for long-duration aerobic sports, high-volume conditioning, and fatigue resistance.
In strength training, prioritize higher-volume hypertrophy and tendon stiffness.

markers.notes: The classic 'Gene for Speed' and the most extensively validated performance polymorphism.

markers.title: PGC-1alpha (Gly482Ser / Mitochondrial Biogenesis)
markers.mechanism: PPARGC1A is the master transcriptional coactivator of mitochondrial biogenesis, oxidative phosphorylation, and muscle fiber-type switching. The T allele (482Ser) reduces PGC-1alpha activity and VO2 max trainability.

CC.label: High Mitochondrial Biogenesis (CC)
CC.summary: Two Gly482 alleles. Robust PGC-1alpha induction upon exercise.
CC.detail: High baseline VO2 max trainability, rapid mitochondrial biogenesis, and superior aerobic adaptation.

move: Thrives with high-volume aerobic conditioning, tempo runs, and cycling.

CT.label: Intermediate Mitochondrial Response (CT)
CT.summary: One 482Ser allele. Balanced aerobic adaptation.
CT.detail: Consistent aerobic training.

TT.label: Reduced Aerobic Trainability (TT)
TT.summary: Two 482Ser alleles. Slower mitochondrial biogenesis adaptation.
TT.detail: May require higher training frequency or specific polarized training models to stimulate equivalent aerobic capacity.

move: Utilize polarized training (80% Zone 2, 20% high-intensity VO2 max intervals) to maximize mitochondrial stimulus.

markers.title: Collagen Type I Alpha 1 (Sp1 Binding Site / Ligament & Bone)
markers.mechanism: COL1A1 encodes the major component of Type I collagen in tendons, ligaments, and bone matrix. The A allele (s allele) increases transcription of alpha-1 chains, leading to an abnormal alpha1/alpha2 chain ratio, reducing tendon tensile strength and bone mineral density.

AA.label: Typical Collagen Architecture (CC / SS)
AA.summary: Normal balanced collagen alpha-1 and alpha-2 chain stoichiometry.
AA.detail: Standard tendon tensile strength and normal baseline cruciate ligament injury risk.

move: Standard athletic training and progressive overload.

AC.label: Intermediate Tendon / Bone Sensitivity (AC / Ss)
AC.summary: One A allele. Slightly altered collagen fibril diameter.
AC.detail: Moderately increased risk of soft-tissue ligament sprains (ACL, Achilles tendon) and slightly lower bone mineral density.

move: Incorporate dedicated eccentric tendon loading (Achilles, patellar) and plyometric landing mechanics.
Ensure progressive loading without sudden volume spikes.
eat: Adequate dietary vitamin C, copper, and collagen/glycine support connective tissue synthesis.

CC.label: High Ligament & Tendon Tear Risk (AA / ss)
CC.summary: Two A alleles. Significant alteration in collagen fiber cross-linking.
CC.detail: Elevated susceptibility to cruciate ligament (ACL) tears, tendon ruptures, and stress fractures during high-impact sports.

move: Rigorous neuromuscular and proprioceptive training (deceleration mechanics, hip stability).
Prioritize slow, heavy eccentric resistance training to stimulate tendon remodeling.
eat: Ensure optimal calcium, vitamin D, and protein intake for bone density.

markers.notes: A critical marker for sports injury prevention and orthopedic risk management.

markers.title: Collagen Type V Alpha 1 (Flexibility vs Running Economy)
markers.mechanism: COL5A1 regulates collagen fibril diameter in tendons. The T allele is associated with stiffer tendons (superior running economy in runners, but lower joint flexibility), whereas C is associated with higher flexibility and increased soft-tissue injury risk.

CC.label: High Tendon Stiffness / Running Economy (TT)
CC.summary: Two T alleles. Denser, stiffer tendon collagen architecture.
CC.detail: Superior elastic energy return and running economy in endurance sports; lower risk of tendon injuries, but reduced range of motion.

move: Ideal for distance running; include mobility and dynamic stretching.

CT.label: Balanced Tendon Mechanics (CT)
CT.summary: One C and one T allele. Balanced flexibility and tendon stiffness.
CT.detail: Normal training.

TT.label: High Flexibility / Soft Tissue Injury Risk (CC)
TT.summary: Two C alleles. Higher joint range of motion and ligament laxity.
TT.detail: Predisposed to muscle cramps, Achilles tendinopathy, and ligament sprains.

move: Emphasize joint stabilization exercises and progressive tendon strengthening.

markers.title: Adenosine Monophosphate Deaminase 1 (G34T / Muscle Fatigue)
markers.mechanism: AMPD1 converts AMP to IMP in skeletal muscle during high-intensity exercise, regulating the purine nucleotide cycle. The A allele (34T) is a nonsense mutation causing myoadenylate deaminase deficiency, leading to early exercise-induced muscle fatigue and cramping.

AA.label: Normal Muscle Energetics (GG)
AA.summary: Full AMPD1 enzyme activity.
AA.detail: Normal ATP regeneration during sprint exercise.

AG.label: Intermediate AMPD1 (AG)
AG.summary: One null allele. Mildly reduced purine nucleotide flux.
AG.detail: May experience slightly longer recovery times between maximal sprint efforts.

move: Allow full rest intervals between maximal sprint sets.

GG.label: AMPD1 Deficiency / Early Fatigue (AA)
GG.summary: Two null alleles. Marked skeletal muscle AMP deaminase deficiency.
GG.detail: Causes premature muscle fatigue, burning sensation, and prolonged muscle cramping during high-intensity anaerobic exercise.

move: Emphasize aerobic pacing and extended recovery intervals between explosive sets.
Supplementation with ribose or beta-alanine may support energy substrate replenishment.

markers.title: Mitochondrial Superoxide Dismutase 2 (Ala16Val / Oxidative Defense)
markers.mechanism: SOD2 (MnSOD) is the primary antioxidant enzyme neutralizing superoxide radicals inside mitochondria. The G allele (Ala16) ensures efficient mitochondrial import, producing high baseline enzyme activity; the A allele (Val16) produces less active enzyme.

AA.label: High Mitochondrial SOD2 (GG / Ala-Ala)
AA.summary: Two Ala alleles. Efficient enzyme import into mitochondria.
AA.detail: High baseline neutralization of exercise-induced and metabolic superoxide radicals.

eat: Maintain balanced dietary antioxidants without over-supplementing high-dose synthetic vitamins.

AG.label: Balanced Oxidative Defense (AG / Ala-Val)
AG.summary: Intermediate SOD2 enzyme activity.
AG.detail: Balanced antioxidant response.

GG.label: Lower Mitochondrial SOD2 (AA / Val-Val)
GG.summary: Two Val alleles. Slower mitochondrial SOD2 import and lower superoxide clearance.
GG.detail: Higher susceptibility to mitochondrial oxidative stress during heavy training or environmental toxic exposure.

eat: Rich dietary intake of colorful polyphenols, berries, sulfur foods (cruciferous, alliums), and green tea.

markers.title: Vitamin D Binding Protein (DBP / Circulating 25-OH D)
markers.mechanism: GC encodes Vitamin D Binding Protein, the primary carrier of 25-hydroxyvitamin D in circulation. The C allele is strongly associated with lower serum 25-OH vitamin D concentrations.

AA.label: Typical Vitamin D Carrier Capacity (AA)
AA.summary: Normal DBP affinity and circulating vitamin D levels.
AA.detail: Standard dietary needs.

AC.label: Moderate Reduction in 25-OH D (AC)
AC.summary: One C allele. Moderately lower circulating 25-OH vitamin D.
AC.detail: May require slightly higher vitamin D intake to achieve optimal blood concentrations (40–60 ng/mL).

vitamins: Ensure regular sun exposure or 1,000–2,000 IU/day Vitamin D3 with K2.

CC.label: Lower Baseline Circulating Vitamin D (CC)
CC.summary: Two C alleles. Significantly lower serum 25-OH D levels.
CC.detail: High risk of seasonal vitamin D insufficiency, particularly at northern latitudes or with indoor lifestyles.

vitamins: Test serum 25-OH Vitamin D via lab panel.
Supplement with Vitamin D3 (2,000–4,000 IU/day) paired with Vitamin K2 and magnesium for proper absorption.

markers.title: Vitamin D 25-Hydroxylase (Hepatic Activation)
markers.mechanism: CYP2R1 converts cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3) into active 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 in the liver. The G allele is associated with lower hepatic hydroxylation efficiency.

AA.label: Typical 25-Hydroxylation (AA)
AA.summary: Efficient hepatic conversion to 25-OH D3.
AA.detail: Normal baseline.

AG.label: Heterozygote (AG)
AG.summary: Intermediate hepatic conversion.
AG.detail: Standard vitamin D support.

GG.label: Reduced Hepatic Activation (GG)
GG.summary: Lower 25-hydroxylase activity.
GG.detail: Requires higher oral D3 doses to achieve target blood levels.

vitamins: Monitor blood levels and pair vitamin D with dietary fats for absorption.

markers.title: Vitamin D Receptor (FokI / C>T)
markers.mechanism: The FokI polymorphism in VDR alters the start codon. The C allele produces a shorter protein (424 AA) with higher transcriptional activity; the T allele produces a longer protein (427 AA) with lower transcriptional efficiency.

CT.label: Intermediate VDR Activity (CT)
CT.summary: Balanced receptor activity.
CT.detail: Standard baseline.

TT.label: Lower VDR Transcriptional Activity (TT)
TT.summary: Longer VDR isoform with reduced transcriptional potency.
TT.detail: Cells may require higher circulating 25-OH D to achieve optimal downstream immune and bone gene expression.

vitamins: Maintain circulating 25-OH D in the robust 40–60 ng/mL range.

markers.title: Beta-Carotene Oxygenase 1 (R267S / Plant Vitamin A Conversion)
markers.mechanism: BCMO1 cleaves dietary provitamin A carotenoids (beta-carotene from carrots, sweet potatoes, spinach) into active retinal (Vitamin A). The T allele (267S) reduces cleavage activity by ~32%, and paired with A379V (rs12934922) reduces conversion by up to ~60–70%.

CC.label: Efficient Carotene Conversion (CC)
CC.detail: Standard conversion of plant carotenoids to active vitamin A.

CT.label: Reduced Carotene Conversion (CT)
CT.summary: One T allele. ~30% reduction in beta-carotene to retinol conversion.
CT.detail: Plant-based carotenoids are converted less efficiently into active preformed vitamin A.

eat: Incorporate preformed vitamin A (retinol) from animal foods (pastured egg yolks, dairy, wild fish, liver) or ensure high total carotenoid intake.

TT.label: Poor Carotenoid Converter (TT)
TT.summary: Two T alleles. ~60% reduction in beta-carotene conversion.
TT.detail: Cannot rely solely on plant carotenoids (carrots/spinach) for adequate vitamin A status; high carotenoid diets may cause carotenemia (orange palms).

eat: Crucial to consume preformed Vitamin A (retinol) directly: pastured egg yolks, grass-fed butter, cod liver oil, or salmon.

markers.notes: A vital marker for individuals following strict vegan or plant-based diets.

markers.title: Fucosyltransferase 2 (Secretor Status / B12 & Gut Microbiome)
markers.mechanism: FUT2 determines 'Secretor' status—the secretion of ABO blood group antigens into mucosal secretions. The A allele (W154X null allele) confers 'Non-Secretor' status (AA), which alters the gut microbiome, lowers circulating Vitamin B12, but confers high resistance to Norovirus.

AA.label: Secretor Phenotype (GG)
AA.summary: Full FUT2 expression. Secretes blood group antigens in gut mucosa.
AA.detail: Optimal Bifidobacteria colonization; standard vitamin B12 absorption; susceptible to common Norovirus strains.

gut: Standard prebiotic and fiber intake to nourish diverse gut flora.

AG.label: Secretor Heterozygote (AG)
AG.summary: Secretor phenotype.
AG.detail: Normal B12 absorption.

GG.label: Non-Secretor Phenotype (AA)
GG.summary: Two null alleles. Complete Non-Secretor status.
GG.detail: Advantages: High resistance to Norovirus (stomach flu). Vulnerabilities: ~20–30% lower circulating B12 levels, lower Bifidobacteria abundance in the gut, higher risk of dysbiosis.

vitamins: Ensure robust B12 intake and monitor serum B12 / methylmalonic acid.
gut: Prioritize prebiotic fibers (inulin, resistant starch, acacia) and fermented foods to support Bifidobacteria.

markers.title: Fatty Acid Desaturase 1 (Omega-3 EPA/DHA Conversion)
markers.mechanism: FADS1 catalyzes the rate-limiting desaturation step converting plant ALA (flax, chia, walnuts) into long-chain anti-inflammatory EPA and DHA. The T allele is associated with significantly lower conversion efficiency.

CC.label: Efficient Omega-3 Converter (CC)
CC.detail: Effective endogenous conversion of plant ALA to EPA.

CT.label: Intermediate Desaturase (CT)
CT.summary: Intermediate conversion efficiency.
CT.detail: Include preformed marine omega-3s.

TT.label: Poor Omega-3 Converter (TT)
TT.summary: Two T alleles. Low FADS1 conversion velocity.
TT.detail: Extremely poor conversion of plant ALA into active EPA and DHA. Plant omega-3 sources (flax/chia) cannot maintain adequate cellular omega-3 index.

eat: Direct consumption of preformed EPA/DHA is essential: wild fatty fish (salmon, sardines, mackerel) or marine algae oil supplements (target 1,000–2,000 mg EPA/DHA daily).

markers.title: Hemochromatosis C282Y (Severe Iron Overload)
markers.mechanism: HFE regulates hepcidin production and cellular iron uptake. The A allele (C282Y) causes hereditary hemochromatosis Type 1, leading to unregulated intestinal iron absorption and progressive iron deposition in the liver, heart, and pancreas.

AA.label: Typical Iron Homeostasis (GG)
AA.summary: No C282Y mutation detected.
AA.detail: Normal baseline iron regulation.

AG.label: HFE C282Y Carrier (AG)
AG.summary: One C282Y allele. ~10–12% of European ancestry individuals are carriers.
AG.detail: Mildly increased iron absorption; ferritin may run high-normal. Men and postmenopausal women should avoid iron-fortified supplements unless deficiency is documented.

eat: Avoid unnecessary iron supplements or high-dose vitamin C paired with red meat (vitamin C enhances iron absorption).
recover: Include serum ferritin and transferrin saturation in routine annual blood work.

GG.label: HFE C282Y Homozygote / Hemochromatosis Risk (AA)
GG.summary: Two C282Y alleles. High risk for clinical Hereditary Hemochromatosis.
GG.detail: Progressive iron accumulation leading to joint pain, liver fibrosis, diabetes ('bronze diabetes'), and cardiomyopathy if untreated.

eat: Strictly avoid all iron supplements, multivitamin iron, cast-iron cooking, and raw shellfish (Vibrio vulnificus vulnerability).
recover: Clinical consultation essential: regular therapeutic phlebotomy (blood donation) completely prevents all organ damage if started early.

markers.notes: The premier genetic screen for preventable hereditary iron overload.

markers.title: Hemochromatosis H63D (Mild Iron Overload)
markers.mechanism: The G allele (H63D) is a milder HFE variant. Compound heterozygotes (C282Y + H63D) have a moderate risk of clinical iron overload.

CG.label: H63D Carrier (CG)
CG.summary: One H63D allele. Very mild effect in isolation.
CG.detail: Check ferritin if paired with C282Y.

GG.label: H63D Homozygote (GG)
GG.summary: Two H63D alleles. Mildly elevated iron absorption.
GG.detail: Ferritin may run higher than average; monitor with standard labs.

eat: Avoid gratuitous iron supplements.

markers.title: Matriptase-2 (A736V / Iron Deficiency & Ferritin Regulator)
markers.mechanism: TMPRSS6 inhibits hepcidin to allow iron absorption. The T allele (736V) impairs matriptase-2, resulting in higher hepcidin levels, lower dietary iron absorption, and lower baseline ferritin.

CT.label: Intermediate (CT)
CT.summary: Balanced iron absorption.
CT.detail: Standard nutrition.

TT.label: Lower Baseline Ferritin (TT)
TT.summary: Two T alleles. Higher baseline hepcidin and reduced dietary iron absorption.
TT.detail: Prone to unexplained low ferritin and iron-deficiency anemia, particularly in menstruating women and endurance athletes.

eat: Pair non-heme iron foods with Vitamin C to enhance absorption; consume bioavailable heme iron (meat/fish) if ferritin is low.

markers.title: Diamine Oxidase (DAO / Histamine Breakdown in Gut)
markers.mechanism: AOC1 encodes Diamine Oxidase (DAO), the primary digestive enzyme that degrades ingested histamine in the intestinal lumen. The T allele reduces DAO enzyme activity, leading to histamine intolerance symptoms (headaches, flushing, nasal congestion, bloating, hives after aged or fermented foods).

CC.label: Normal DAO Activity (CC)
CC.summary: Full DAO expression in intestinal mucosa.

CT.label: Reduced DAO Activity (CT)
CT.summary: One T allele. Moderately reduced luminal histamine breakdown.
CT.detail: Sensitive to high-histamine food combinations (aged cheese + red wine + cured meats).

eat: Moderate consumption of aged cheeses, wine, fermented foods, and cured meats if symptoms occur.

TT.label: High Histamine Intolerance Susceptibility (TT)
TT.summary: Two T alleles. Significantly reduced DAO enzyme production.
TT.detail: High susceptibility to dietary histamine overload: flushing, post-meal brain fog, migraine triggers, and digestive distress.

eat: Follow a low-histamine dietary approach: prioritize fresh meats, avoid aged/fermented foods, leftovers, canned fish, and alcohol.
DAO enzyme supplements taken before meals can assist in degrading dietary histamine.

markers.notes: Primary genetic locus for gut-mediated histamine intolerance.

markers.title: Lactase Persistence (-13910C>T / Adult Dairy Tolerance)
markers.mechanism: rs4988235 in MCM6 is the master regulatory switch for the LCT gene. In ancestral humans, lactase shuts off after weaning (Lactase Non-Persistence / CC). The T allele keeps lactase production active into adulthood (Lactase Persistence / CT or TT).

CC.label: Lactase Persistent (TT)
CC.summary: Two persistence alleles. Lifelong high intestinal lactase production.
CC.detail: Full capability to digest milk sugar (lactose) throughout adulthood without bloating or digestive symptoms.

eat: Can consume regular milk, yogurt, and dairy products without lactose-related intolerance.

CT.label: Lactase Persistent Heterozygote (CT)
CT.summary: One persistence allele. Sustained adult lactase production.
CT.detail: Tolerates standard dairy products well.

eat: Standard dairy tolerance.

TT.label: Lactase Non-Persistent / Lactose Intolerant (CC)
TT.summary: Two ancestral alleles. Adult decline in lactase enzyme expression.
TT.detail: Ingestion of unfermented milk sugar (lactose) leads to microbial fermentation, bloating, gas, and osmotic diarrhea.
