eat: Choose naturally lactose-free dairy (hard cheeses, butter), fermented dairy (kefir, Greek yogurt), lactose-free milk, or use lactase enzyme drops.

markers.notes: The classic human evolutionary selective sweep for adult pastoralism.

markers.title: Bitter Taste Receptor (PAV / AVI Bitter Sensitivity)
markers.mechanism: TAS2R38 governs sensitivity to glucosinolates and thiourea compounds (PTC/PROP) found in cruciferous vegetables (broccoli, kale, Brussels sprouts) and coffee. C corresponds to the taster (Proline/P) allele; G to non-taster (Alanine/A).

CC.label: Super-Taster Allele (CC / PAV)
CC.summary: Two bitter taster alleles. Intense perception of glucosinolate bitterness.
CC.detail: Cruciferous vegetables (kale, broccoli, cabbage), black coffee, and tonic water taste intensely bitter.

eat: Cook crucifers with healthy fats (olive oil, butter), sea salt, and acids (lemon/vinegar) to neutralize the bitter receptor binding.
Do not skip brassicas—prepare them properly.

GG.label: Non-Taster (GG / AVI)
GG.summary: Two non-taster alleles. Dulled bitter perception.
GG.detail: Cruciferous vegetables and coffee taste mild and sweet.

eat: Naturally tolerates raw cruciferous vegetables.

markers.title: Interleukin-6 Promoter (-174G>C / Systemic Inflammation)
markers.mechanism: IL-6 is a key pro-inflammatory cytokine and exercise-induced myokine. The G allele is associated with higher inducible IL-6 expression in response to stress and exercise.

CC.label: Higher Inducible IL-6 (GG)
CC.summary: Two G alleles. Robust IL-6 inflammatory response.
CC.detail: Higher systemic inflammatory reactivity, but also strong myokine signaling during resistance training.

eat: Anti-inflammatory nutrition: high omega-3s, curcumin, dark berries, and leafy greens.
move: Ensure adequate recovery days between intense training sessions.

GG.label: Lower Inducible IL-6 (CC)
GG.summary: Two C alleles. Lower baseline IL-6 production.
GG.detail: Associated with lower baseline systemic inflammation and favorable cardiovascular longevity profiles.

eat: Standard healthy anti-inflammatory diet.

markers.title: Tumor Necrosis Factor-Alpha (-308G>A)
markers.mechanism: TNF-alpha is a central master cytokine driving acute and chronic inflammation. The A allele (-308A) increases TNF-alpha promoter transcription by ~2-fold.

AA.label: Typical TNF-Alpha (GG)
AA.summary: Standard baseline TNF-alpha transcription.
AA.detail: Normal inflammatory baseline.

AG.label: Elevated TNF-Alpha Expression (AG)
AG.summary: One A allele. Higher inducible TNF-alpha expression.
AG.detail: Predisposed to stronger inflammatory reactions, post-infection fatigue, and inflammatory joint discomfort.

eat: Incorporate natural TNF-alpha modulators: curcumin, green tea EGCG, ginger, and EPA/DHA omega-3s.

GG.label: High TNF-Alpha Transcription (AA)
GG.summary: Two A alleles. Markedly higher inducible TNF-alpha.
GG.detail: Significant pro-inflammatory tendency; benefits from proactive lifestyle anti-inflammatory protocols.

eat: Strict whole-food anti-inflammatory diet; avoid industrial seed oils and refined sugars.
mind: Chronic psychological stress elevates TNF-alpha; practice active stress reduction.

markers.title: HLA-B*27 Tag SNP (Ankylosing Spondylitis & Reactive Arthritis)
markers.mechanism: rs4349859 is in strong linkage disequilibrium with the HLA-B*27 major histocompatibility complex antigen, the strongest genetic risk factor for axial spondyloarthritis (Ankylosing Spondylitis), uveitis, and reactive arthritis.

AA.label: Typical (GG)
AA.summary: Negative for HLA-B*27 tag.
AA.detail: Low baseline genetic risk for HLA-B27 associated arthropathies.

AG.label: HLA-B*27 Tag Carrier (AG)
AG.summary: One A allele. Positive tag for HLA-B*27.
AG.detail: Associated with increased lifetime susceptibility to inflammatory back pain (axial spondyloarthritis), uveitis, and reactive arthritis. Most carriers never develop disease, but early recognition of inflammatory back pain is crucial.

move: Maintain daily spinal mobility, swimming, and postural exercises.
recover: If experiencing chronic inflammatory lower back/sacroiliac pain that improves with exercise but worsens with rest, consult a rheumatologist.

GG.label: HLA-B*27 Tag Homozygote (AA)
GG.summary: Two A alleles. Positive for HLA-B*27.
GG.detail: Elevated susceptibility to HLA-B27 spondyloarthropathies.

recover: Discuss with a clinician if joint inflammation or eye inflammation (uveitis) occurs.

markers.title: Lymphoid Phosphatase (R620W / Multi-Autoimmune Susceptibility)
markers.mechanism: PTPN22 (Lyp) regulates T-cell and B-cell receptor signaling thresholds. The A allele (620W) impairs phosphatase inhibition, allowing autoreactive immune cells to escape negative selection, predisposing to multiple autoimmune conditions (Hashimoto's thyroiditis, Type 1 diabetes, rheumatoid arthritis, vitiligo).

AA.label: Typical Immune Signaling (GG)
AA.summary: Normal T-cell receptor threshold.
AA.detail: Baseline autoimmune risk.

AG.label: Autoimmune Susceptibility Carrier (AG)
AG.summary: One A allele. ~2x increased risk for autoimmune thyroid and joint conditions.
AG.detail: Lower threshold for autoreactive immune activation.

eat: Prioritize gut barrier integrity: avoid ultra-processed emulsifiers, optimize vitamin D, and maintain a diverse microbiome.
recover: Include thyroid panel (TSH, free T4, TPO antibodies) in annual checkups if autoimmune symptoms arise.

GG.label: High Autoimmune Susceptibility (AA)
GG.summary: Two A alleles. Significantly increased multi-autoimmune predisposition.
GG.detail: Elevated lifetime vigilance for autoimmune presentations.

recover: Annual autoimmune screening and prompt evaluation of persistent unexplained fatigue or joint pain.

markers.title: Forkhead Box O3 (Centenarian Longevity Factor)
markers.mechanism: FOXO3 is a master transcriptional regulator of autophagy, DNA repair, antioxidant enzymes, and stem cell homeostasis. The G allele is heavily enriched in centenarians worldwide (2- to 3-fold higher prevalence in individuals living >100 years).

GG.label: Centenarian Longevity Allele Homozygote (GG)
GG.summary: Two G alleles. Maximized FOXO3-mediated stress resilience.
GG.detail: Enhanced cellular autophagy, superior DNA damage repair, and reduced cardiovascular mortality across lifespan studies.

longevity: Autophagy-inducing lifestyle practices (intermittent fasting, sauna, exercise) synergize powerfully with FOXO3 activation.

GT.label: Longevity Allele Carrier (GT)
GT.summary: One G allele. Robust FOXO3 activation.
GT.detail: Associated with healthy cellular aging and cardiovascular protection.

longevity: Regular physical activity and caloric balance maintain FOXO3 pathway signaling.

TT.label: Typical FOXO3 (TT)
TT.summary: Two T alleles. Standard baseline FOXO3 expression.
TT.detail: Standard cellular repair dynamics; fully responsive to healthy lifestyle habits.

markers.notes: The single most replicated genetic longevity locus across diverse global cohorts.

markers.title: Telomerase Reverse Transcriptase (Telomere Length Maintenance)
markers.mechanism: TERT encodes the catalytic subunit of telomerase, which maintains telomere length at chromosome ends during cellular division. The A allele is associated with longer leukocyte telomere length.

AA.label: Longer Telomere Maintenance (AA)
AA.summary: Two A alleles. Superior telomere length preservation.
AA.detail: Favorable cellular replicative capacity.

AG.label: Intermediate (AG)
AG.summary: Balanced telomere dynamics.
AG.detail: Standard baseline.

GG.label: Shorter Telomere Tendency (GG)
GG.summary: Two G alleles. Moderately shorter baseline leukocyte telomeres.
GG.detail: Cellular aging is more sensitive to chronic psychological stress and smoking.

longevity: Stress management, aerobic exercise, and Mediterranean diet are clinically proven to preserve telomere length.

markers.title: Aldehyde Dehydrogenase 2 (Glu504Lys / Asian Alcohol Flush)
markers.mechanism: ALDH2 breaks down carcinogenic acetaldehyde into harmless acetate. The A allele (ALDH2*2 / 504Lys) is a dominant negative mutation that abolishes enzyme activity (~80% loss in GA, >95% loss in AA), causing severe toxic acetaldehyde accumulation after alcohol (flushing, nausea, tachycardia, high esophageal cancer risk).

AA.label: ALDH2*2 Homozygote / Severe Acetaldehyde Toxicity (AA)
AA.summary: Two *2 null alleles. Near-complete absence of mitochondrial ALDH2 activity.
AA.detail: Severe facial flushing, nausea, headache, and tachycardia after even sips of alcohol. Acetaldehyde is a potent DNA mutagen.

substances: Strictly avoid all alcoholic beverages. Alcohol is highly toxic to your biology.

AG.label: Alcohol Flush Carrier / ALDH2*2 Heterozygote (AG)
AG.summary: One *2 allele. ~80% reduction in acetaldehyde clearance velocity.
AG.detail: Classic Asian flush reaction: rapid facial redness, palpitations, and elevated risk of upper gastrointestinal cancers if alcohol is consumed.

substances: Strong recommendation to eliminate or severely restrict alcohol. Never take antihistamines to 'mask' the flush, which increases cancer risk.

GG.label: Normal Alcohol Metabolism (GG)
GG.summary: Two *1 alleles. Fully functional ALDH2 enzyme.
GG.detail: Normal acetaldehyde clearance.

markers.notes: A critical public health pharmacogenomic and oncologic marker.

markers.title: Alcohol Dehydrogenase 1B (Arg48His / Fast Ethanol Conversion)
markers.mechanism: ADH1B converts ethanol into acetaldehyde. The T allele (48His / *2) accelerates ethanol oxidation by ~40–80x, rapidly generating acetaldehyde and conferring strong natural protection against alcohol dependence.

CC.label: Rapid Ethanol Conversion / Alcohol Protection (TT)
CC.summary: Two *2 alleles. Extremely rapid conversion of alcohol to acetaldehyde.
CC.detail: High natural resistance to alcohol dependence and alcoholism.

substances: Natural biological deterrent against alcohol overconsumption.

CT.label: Intermediate Conversion (CT)
CT.summary: One *2 allele. Accelerated alcohol metabolism.
CT.detail: Protective against heavy drinking.

TT.label: Standard Alcohol Dehydrogenase (CC)
TT.summary: Standard ADH1B rate.
TT.detail: Standard baseline.

markers.title: ATP-Binding Cassette C11 (538G>A / Dry Earwax & Body Odor)
markers.mechanism: ABCC11 encodes an apocrine gland transporter. The A allele (538A) is a loss-of-function mutation causing dry/flaky earwax and the complete absence of axillary body odor (no apocrine sweat secretion of odor precursors). Highly prevalent in East Asians (>80%).

AA.label: Dry Earwax & Zero Underarm Odor (AA)
AA.summary: Two A alleles. Complete loss of apocrine axillary odor secretion.
AA.detail: Produces dry, grayish earwax and eliminates the genetic requirement for underarm deodorant.

traits: Naturally free of apocrine body odor; no clinical need for aluminum antiperspirants.

AG.label: Wet Earwax & Standard Body Odor (AG)
AG.summary: One G allele. Functional apocrine secretion.
AG.detail: Produces wet earwax and typical body odor.

GG.label: Wet Earwax & Standard Body Odor (GG)
GG.summary: Two G alleles. Standard apocrine gland secretion.
GG.detail: Standard baseline.

markers.title: Iris & Hair Pigmentation Switch (Blue vs Brown Eyes)
markers.mechanism: rs12913832 in the HERC2 intron acts as the master enhancer switch regulating the promoter of OCA2. The G allele disrupts the chromatin loop, drastically reducing OCA2 expression in the iris stroma, leading to blue/gray/green eyes.

AA.label: Blue / Gray / Light Green Eyes (GG)
AA.summary: Two G alleles. Suppressed OCA2 expression in iris melanocytes.

GG.detail: Predictive of brown or dark brown eyes.

markers.title: Melanocortin 1 Receptor (Arg151Cys / Red Hair & Sun Sensitivity)
markers.mechanism: MC1R regulates the switch between dark eumelanin and red/yellow pheomelanin in melanocytes. The T allele (151Cys / 'R' allele) is a major loss-of-function variant causing red hair, fair skin, freckling, and high sunburn/melanoma susceptibility.

traits: Use daily sun protection and avoid deliberate tanning bed exposure.

TT.label: Typical Tanning Capability (CC)
TT.summary: No Arg151Cys variant detected.
TT.detail: Normal baseline melanogenesis.

markers.title: Ectodysplasin A Receptor (370A / Hair Thickness & Tooth Morphology)
markers.mechanism: EDAR 370A (G allele) is an adaptive mutation that arose ~30,000 years ago in East Asia. It increases EDAR signaling, producing significantly thicker hair fibers, shovel-shaped incisors, and altered mammary and sweat gland branching.

AA.label: East Asian Adaptive Phenotype / Thick Hair (GG)

GG.label: Ancestral Thin/Medium Hair (AA)
GG.summary: Ancestral EDAR signaling.
GG.detail: Standard hair shaft diameter.

markers.title: Olfactory Receptor 6A2 (Cilantro / Coriander Soap Taste)
markers.mechanism: OR6A2 detects aldehyde odorants. The A allele enhances binding to (2E)-alkenals found in cilantro leaves, making cilantro taste intensely of dish soap or bath soap.

AA.label: Strong Cilantro Soapy Taste (AA)
AA.summary: Two A alleles. Highly sensitized aldehyde olfactory receptor.
AA.detail: Fresh cilantro/coriander tastes overwhelmingly soapy and pungent.

CC.label: Herbaceous Cilantro Taste (CC)
CC.detail: Perceives cilantro as fresh, citrusy, and herbaceous.

markers.title: Leucine-Rich Repeat Kinase 2 (G2019S / Parkinson's Risk Tag)
markers.mechanism: LRRK2 G2019S is the most common genetic contributor to familial and sporadic Parkinson's disease (incomplete penetrance ~25–30% by age 80).

GG.label: Homozygote (AA)

markers.title: Beta-Fibrinogen (-455G>A / Elevated Fibrinogen)
markers.mechanism: FGB encodes the beta chain of fibrinogen. The A allele (-455A) elevates basal and IL-6-induced plasma fibrinogen levels, increasing blood viscosity and thrombotic risk.

AA.label: Typical Fibrinogen (GG)
AA.summary: Standard fibrinogen expression.
AA.detail: Normal baseline plasma viscosity.

AG.label: Elevated Fibrinogen Carrier (AG)
AG.summary: One A allele. Moderately elevated circulating fibrinogen.
AG.detail: Higher blood viscosity and inflammatory clotting reactivity.

markers.title: Paraoxonase 1 (Q192R / HDL Antioxidant Capacity)
markers.mechanism: PON1 is an HDL-associated esterase that protects LDL and HDL from oxidative modification and hydrolyzes organophosphates. The G allele (192R) has higher paraoxonase activity but lower efficiency in metabolizing lipid peroxides.

AA.label: High Peroxide Hydrolysis (AA / 192Q)
AA.summary: Two Q alleles. Superior protection against oxidized LDL.
AA.detail: High endogenous antioxidant protection for HDL.

GG.summary: Two R alleles. Lower efficiency in detoxifying lipid peroxides.
GG.detail: May benefit from higher dietary polyphenol intake (extra virgin olive oil, pomegranate, green tea) to preserve HDL quality.

eat: Incorporate rich dietary polyphenols and extra virgin olive oil to enhance PON1 expression.

markers.title: Platelet Glycoprotein IIIa (PlA1/PlA2 / Pro-Thrombotic Platelets)
markers.mechanism: ITGB3 forms the platelet fibrinogen receptor GPIIb/IIIa. The C allele (PlA2 / Leu33Pro) increases platelet aggregability and thrombotic risk.

CT.label: Hyper-Reactive Platelet Carrier (CT / PlA2)
CT.summary: One PlA2 allele. Moderately enhanced platelet reactivity.
CT.detail: Slightly higher risk of arterial thrombosis under endothelial shear stress.

TT.label: High Platelet Reactivity (CC / PlA2)
TT.summary: Two PlA2 alleles. Hyper-reactive platelet aggregation.
TT.detail: Higher risk of acute coronary syndrome; discuss antiplatelet strategies with a physician.

recover: Clinical consultation if cardiovascular disease or stent placement is relevant.

markers.title: Apolipoprotein C3 (3238C>G / SstI / Hypertriglyceridemia)
markers.mechanism: APOC3 inhibits lipoprotein lipase and hepatic uptake of triglyceride-rich particles. The G allele increases APOC3 expression, leading to elevated plasma triglycerides.

CG.label: Elevated Triglyceride Risk (CG)
CG.summary: One G allele. Moderately higher circulating triglycerides.
CG.detail: Sensitive to high-carbohydrate and alcohol intake.

eat: Limit refined sugars, high-fructose corn syrup, and alcohol; emphasize EPA/DHA omega-3s.

GG.label: High Hypertriglyceridemia Susceptibility (GG)
GG.summary: Two G alleles. Significantly reduced triglyceride clearance.
GG.detail: Predisposed to high fasting triglycerides and remnant cholesterol.

eat: Strict low-sugar, low-alcohol diet; high-dose marine omega-3s (2–3g/day EPA/DHA) effectively lower triglycerides.
recover: Monitor fasting lipid panel with advanced particle testing.

markers.title: Lipoprotein Lipase (Ser447Ter / Cardioprotective Variant)
markers.mechanism: LPL hydrolyzes triglycerides in chylomicrons and VLDL. The G allele (447Ter) is a premature stop codon that creates a super-active LPL enzyme, leading to lower plasma triglycerides and higher HDL-C.

CG.label: Enhanced Triglyceride Clearance / Cardioprotective (CG)
CG.summary: One 447Ter allele. ~15–20% lower plasma triglycerides and higher HDL.
CG.detail: Conveys natural genetic protection against coronary artery disease.

eat: Maintain balanced healthy fats; excellent genetic buffer for triglyceride clearance.

GG.label: Super-Active LPL Homozygote (GG)
GG.summary: Two 447Ter alleles. Rapid triglyceride clearance and elevated HDL-C.
GG.detail: Significant lifetime cardioprotection.

markers.title: CYP2D6*10 Reduced Function (100C>T / Pro34Ser)
markers.mechanism: CYP2D6*10 is the predominant reduced-function allele in East Asian populations (~40–50% allele frequency). It reduces enzymatic clearance of beta-blockers, antidepressants, and antiarrhythmics.

CT.label: CYP2D6*10 Carrier / Intermediate Metabolizer (CT)
CT.summary: One *10 allele. Moderately reduced CYP2D6 clearance.
CT.detail: CPIC Guideline: Slower clearance of metoprolol, flecainide, and codeine.

recover: Review with doctor when dosing CYP2D6-metabolized medications.

TT.label: CYP2D6*10 Homozygote / Intermediate Metabolizer (TT)
TT.summary: Two *10 alleles. Significantly reduced CYP2D6 activity.
TT.detail: Common in East Asia; standard doses of psychotropics or beta-blockers produce higher serum drug levels.

recover: Discuss dose titration with a prescribing clinician.

markers.title: CYP3A5*3 Splicing Defect (6986A>G / Tacrolimus Metabolism)
markers.mechanism: CYP3A5 metabolizes calcineurin inhibitors (Tacrolimus) used in organ transplantation and autoimmune treatment. The G allele (*3) is a splicing defect causing complete lack of CYP3A5 expression (CYP3A5 Non-Expressor).

AA.label: CYP3A5 Expressor / Rapid Clearance (AA)
AA.summary: Two *1 functional alleles. High hepatic and intestinal CYP3A5 expression.
AA.detail: CPIC Guideline: Requires 1.5–2x higher starting doses of tacrolimus to reach therapeutic blood levels.

recover: Critical for immunosuppressive and transplant dosing protocols.

AG.label: CYP3A5 Intermediate Expressor (AG)
AG.summary: One *1 allele. Moderate CYP3A5 expression.
AG.detail: CPIC Guideline: Intermediate tacrolimus dose requirements.

recover: Standard therapeutic drug monitoring.

GG.label: CYP3A5 Non-Expressor (GG / *3/*3)
GG.summary: Two *3 null alleles. Standard Non-Expressor phenotype (~85% of Europeans).
GG.detail: Standard baseline tacrolimus dosing requirements.

recover: Standard clinical monitoring.

markers.title: Thiopurine S-Methyltransferase (TPMT*3C / Tyr240Cys)
markers.mechanism: TPMT*3C is the predominant thiopurine loss-of-function allele in East Asian and African populations.

AA.label: Typical (AA)
AA.summary: Normal TPMT activity.
AA.detail: Standard thiopurine dosing.

AG.label: TPMT*3C Carrier / Intermediate Metabolizer (AG)
AG.summary: One *3C null allele.

GG.label: TPMT*3C Homozygote / Severe Deficiency (GG)
GG.summary: Two *3C null alleles.
GG.detail: CPIC Guideline: Severe thiopurine-induced bone marrow suppression risk.

recover: Mandatory oncology/gastroenterology consultation.
